The other thing was the idea that there’s a lot of problems in the world, and it’s diverting our attention away from those problems. And there’s no way that you could ever convince me that by attending to beauty you become less aware of problems. To me, they are opposite ends of a pole, and when you are in the presence of something beautiful, it’s helping to nourish your recognition of what is intolerable, and cruelty is intolerable. And vice versa. When you see cruelty, you long for, as at Guantánamo, the photograph of the flower. So I think they were incoherent arguments, and I think that they were also mutually exclusive. On the one hand, one argument was saying, “Our acts of vision are destructive. You hurt the thing you’re looking at.” The other argument was that by not looking at something, by ignoring something, you produce harm in it. And even if you go to the locus of the problem, the idea that there are cases, let’s say, when the male gaze is used violently, even then it is something that can’t plausibly be generalized to males looking at women or women looking at men. Because if you go back through time, it’s the perceiver who’s always vulnerable. It’s Dante whose knees are buckling when he sees Beatrice. That occurs all the way down the line. It’s like Sappho’s “Raise high the roof beam, carpenters.” You have to make the doorways taller to accommodate the person. You have to fill the hillside with flowers. It goes back to the earlier conversation we were having about the kind of growth or enlargement of perception that comes by being in the presence of beauty. Brooks: There’s one other argument that the war on beauty folks could wage; I see it in my own profession in journalism. There are two things going on. One is middle-class Americans or the bourgeoisie are overly content, and you need to shock them out of their mediocrity. And the other is that in the media, our theory of change is if we can explain what’s wrong, we’ve done our job. We have a strong bias toward negative news. And we don’t have to explain how to fix it. We just expose the sin. And I think it’s been proven that this approach to promoting social change by shocking people or by reminding them of how awful things are is a pretty rotten way to motivate people to do change. You can’t just say, “This is rotten, this is hopeless, this is terrible.” You have to provide an alternative vision, which is what beauty is—literally an alternative vision. Scarry: I agree with that. In fact, have you seen this new documentary called Josh’s Wedding ? You watch the computer generate its own poem. Then you also see it give its opinion of human beings, which is that we’re contemptible, we’re small, we’re worthless. Perhaps that is just one of 1,000 things that AI would say about human beings. But it suddenly began to make me and Philip Fisher, my life partner, worry: “Wait a minute, these computers are being trained on all these books and newspapers that report only the negative.” For every act of cruelty, there are probably that day a million acts of kindness in the world. The kind of fear that AI might inflict cruelty by unleashing a nuclear weapon or whatever always seemed odd to me, only in the sense of: What would be the motive? But if the picture we have of ourselves is so negative, that might be a reason. Brooks: You published this book, 26 years ago? And when you did it, the anti-beauty movement was at full force. Scarry: I think that’s right. Brooks: What’s the update 26 years later? Scarry: I think that gradually things have been restored. I mean, I see conferences on beauty. I think that students—you know, even in the ’90s I taught this course on beauty, in the ’90s, and certainly students took the course. There are lots of signs that that is much less of a problem. Now, somebody who is in art history told me that that is still the case in art history departments. But I didn’t question him enough to know if that is absolutely the case. I just know that it’s something that I shouldn’t so blithely think, Yeah, we’re out of it now . We’re out of danger now . Maybe we’re not. Brooks: These things take a while. As they say, intellectual history travels by hearse. You have to lose people to lose certain ideas. Well, thank you for this time. I’m reminded of a friend of mine named Jenny McShane, who I’ve known since I was 10, made a movie called The Quilters about guys in a maximum-security prison who quilt. And that’s the center of their life. And they’re in there, they’re never coming out, and they just wanna create beauty. Among people like that, beauty never went out of fashion. Elaine Scarry, thank you so much for joining us on The Permanent Questions . Scarry: Thank you so much for having me. Brooks: I leave this conversation just reminded again that beauty is everywhere. We talk about moral beauty, physical beauty, intellectual beauty, mathematical beauty, a beautiful tennis shot, and I really was persuaded by Elaine that it is all one thing. Beauty is one thing, one sensation of symmetry, of reciprocity, of just something that’s innately pleasurable. I’m also reminded that perception is so much of what we do. We used to have this idea that perception, you just open your eyes and reality floods in, and the real mental action up here was thinking, was cognition, cogitation. But I think we’re understanding as the cognitive sciences bring us along that perception is thinking, and most of our thinking is actually in our perceptions. You don’t have to think about whether you’re seeing a morally admirable act or a morally degrading act. You just see it and you know immediately in the way you know a painting is beautiful or not beautiful. And so I think we got a little glimpse on that process. And then I really walk away persuaded that even though I can think of a lot of artists and poets who are not wonderful human beings, I do think the constant act of experiencing beauty over years, over decades, does enlarge the soul and does make us kinder toward others, more considerate toward others, and greater in our longing for the good. So thanks so much for joining us for this week’s conversation with Elaine Scarry. The Permanent Questions is produced and edited by The Atlantic in partnership with Yale University. New episodes of The Permanent Questions drop each Sunday. You can subscribe on The Atlantic ’s YouTube channel, on Spotify, on Apple, or wherever you get your podcasts. If you wanna support this work and the work of my colleagues, you can subscribe to the publication at TheAtlantic.com/Listener. See you next week. The Permanent Questions is edited by Christopher Beha and produced by Rebecca Davis. This episode was engineered by Miguel Carrascal. Our theme is by Rob Smierciak. Claudine Ebeid is the executive producer of Atlantic audio, and Andrea Valdez is our managing editor.

items.title: The Right Way to Make Mac and Cheese
items.description: My Aunt Louise and my grandmother both smoked Virginia Slims. At social events, even barbecues, Louise’s cigarette was in a theater-length holder. She was married to a loud man we called Uncle Benny, who held his Marlboro in the same hand as his highball. Louise’s kitchen, with its Talavera tile and swinging door, functioned like a VIP suite. It’s where the mac and cheese was made, and the very important people were the kids. This was late-1970s Los Angeles. Louise and Benny lived in a gray Spanish-revival bungalow common to the multiracial Miracle Mile: a red-clay roof and a front courtyard tinkling with chimes. On any given weekend, a hunting pal of Benny’s might stomp onto Louise’s spotless back patio with just-caught cod, or crayfish still moving in the trap—maybe even deer heart, thawing in a ziplock, or fresh pheasant to throw on the grill. It was fine for others to contribute a protein, but side dishes were Louise’s domain: deviled eggs, braised mustard greens, and the mac and cheese for which she was famous. I’d watch Louise fold boiled elbow noodles into the Cracker Barrel Extra Sharp I had shredded, plus eggs beaten with Knudsen whole milk (as opposed to Carnation evaporated). There were other ingredients—a spoonful of dry mustard, a pinch of Tony Chachere’s Original Creole Seasoning—but what stood out to me were Louise’s careful shakes, from a Schilling tin, of cream of tartar. I didn’t know what that was, and I wasn’t alone. For Louise’s clique, cream of tartar was a culinary idiosyncrasy. “Cream of what?” they’d ask. “Why?” Now, decades later, rowdy debates about mac and cheese are all over social media, especially at holiday time. Should mac and cheese be pourable, or baked until it can be cut like brownies? Is truffle a grace note, or too highfalutin? The sparring goes down in TikTok Stitches and the comment sections of Instagram Reels, as creators mix in mozzarella or mascarpone. Home cooks zhuzh up boxes of Kraft. My Haitian American friends make macaroni au gratin with habanero-laced epis . Ina Garten marinates her cooked pasta in cream , as you would overnight oats. I adore a good, melty cube of Velveeta (in my scrambled eggs), but using Campbell’s Condensed Cheddar Cheese Soup? In mac and cheese? Gag me—as we used to say in 1980s Southern California—with a spoon. Alex Hill , an L.A.-based content creator and recipe developer under the name @justaddhotsauce, knows that ingredients and cooking styles go in and out of fashion. She grew up watching her mother learn to make mac and cheese from the singer Patti LaBelle, a best-selling cookbook author whose recipe is a five-cheese stunner (and made in the custard style of my Aunt Louise). Hill’s mom, a Puerto Rican married to a Black American, wanted to make mac and cheese in a way beloved by her husband and his family. “I thought my mom made the best mac and cheese,” Hill, whose own mac is béchamel-based, told me. “She used Velveeta. And now it’s so taboo.” My Aunt Louise was not kin but sister-friend to my maternal grandmother, Lottie. They were glamorous, frank, and 40 years older than me, but Louise spoke about the body in a way that shared DNA often disallows. When I was 12, she told me there was no way to grate cheese without risking the skin of my knuckles. “Stop being so tentative,” Louise said. “As you know, it’s not if you bleed, kiddo. It’s when .” I had thought that the way Louise looked out for me and other children meant that I knew her. I’ll never know how much I didn’t know. My grandmother and her girlfriends came of age in 1940s California, when school segregation was customary (and legal, until ’47). Aunt Louise and Grandma Lottie both married military men and lived through the assassination era. I used to think of these women as always being braced for something. Tense. As we all got older, I could see they were shoring up a broken heart. People in my grandmother’s set rarely talked about their emotions, at least to us. They were who they were because things were the way they were. Like Louise, my grandmother was a good cook who did not love to cook. But Grandma taught me to make a nog so thick with beaten egg whites that it’s eaten with a spoon. When I realized that she didn’t even like the nog, she told me that you don’t have to like something to make it. “You can make it,” she said, “because other people like it.” (I hear this in my head when I make my “famous” peach cobbler that I don’t even like. Compliments are yummy, though, right? Especially when you’re hungry for them.) Cooking for pleasure must have been a complex notion for my grandmother; her mother had cooked for a living in the Piedmont area of Oakland, where Black people were forbidden to be owners or tenants. At one of Louise and Benny’s gatherings—where spatchcocked birds dripped with browned butter, brown sugar, and cayenne—I heard one of Louise’s friends getting nosy about the menu. This friend’s name was Mae or Bea, something one-syllable, and she was among the fools Louise welcomed but did not suffer, when it came to kitchen meddling. Mae (or Bea): You’re not making a roux? Louise: Roux is for gumbo and gravy. Then one of Benny’s crew barreled through the swinging door with charred wild-turkey thighs. Before Louise could block him, the man stuffed a boy’s mouth with a burnt piece, then howled: “That’s a rabbit! That’s the Easter Bunny you just ate!” Now that child was crying. Then another. I wanted to fight this man. But I was 12. In that kitchen, with its undernotes of Clorox, Louise looked up from dotting margarine on the steaming noodles in her rectangular glass pan. She didn’t like grown men “hooting and hollering.” She didn’t like jokes that only the joker found funny. Aunt Louise had spoken to me of the sourness among folks who experienced different levels of possibility, and freedom. This was why she didn’t much like for the generations to mix—unless she was on duty at the velvet rope. So Louise hustled me, my sister, and our pals into her den. She passed me, the oldest, a boxy television remote, then fanned out editions of Ebony , Life , Essence , and Sunset . She brought us a bowl of chips and some mild salsa. Shutting the door as she left, Louise gave us a look that said simply and seriously that this was our territory while treacherous guests were nearby. As usual, I followed her back to the kitchen. I noted how Louise contained the chaos. I was brave before the deer’s heart. I got back to cheese grating. In the summer of 2000, when my sister was getting married, I visited Louise in a nursing home. She was a widow recovering—to the degree that she ever could—from an amputation. I had been living in New York City for seven years, and she acted as if that were a magical distance and length of time. My grandmother had told her I was doing well in my work—that I was, like the Jeffersons, moving on up. With a wink, Louise gave me a bottle of Rive Gauche from her bureau, and then asked me if I still cooked. I said I did, and I was glad it was true. “I think we’re losing recipes,” Alex Hill had said, and for more than mac and cheese. Recipes aren’t just nourishment, nor are they merely strokes of “culture.” They are relationships. They make us feel included and protected. For me, they are loyalty—a sweetness where there might have been bitters. Hill, who has a cookbook coming out next year, knows the necessity of sharing her passions on social media, but she doesn’t want to cook something solely because it might go viral. “I actually want to cook ,” she said. “I want you to cook my recipes.” The elbows in Aunt Louise’s mac and cheese held cooked milk in their curves. My recipe is not the same as Louise’s, but it’s close. I use cream of tartar. I believe roux is for gumbo and gravy. I tilt my glass pan, just as Louise did, to see if any liquid moves. If it doesn’t, I pull it from the oven. The top, crunchy. The edges, brown. Our custard, silky. Alex Hill says cream of tartar is a stabilizer. Louise had told me that too, in her Miracle Mile courtyard. “Cream of tartar has no taste,” she said. “It just holds everything together.” At the time, I didn’t understand. This article appears in the December 2026 print edition with the headline “The Right Way to Make Mac and Cheese .”

items.title: Mandiana : le directeur préfectoral de l’Environnement accusé d’avoir perçu 105 millions GNF pour renoncer à un contrôle minier
items.description: 105 millions de francs guinéens contre l'absence de contrôle. C'est l'accusation grave portée par des responsables locaux de Balandougouba contre le directeur préfectoral de l'Environnement de Mandiana et son équipe, soupçonnés d'avoir monnayé leur mission dans les zones d'exploitation aurifère. Le mis en cause rejette en bloc et menace de porter plainte. Une affaire de corruption présumée secoue la sous-préfecture de Balandougouba, dans la préfecture de Mandiana. Au cœur de la controverse : une somme de 105 millions de francs guinéens qui aurait été collectée auprès de plusieurs villages à la suite de discussions avec une mission du service préfectoral de l'Environnement. Selon les témoignages recueillis auprès d'un participant aux discussions et du maire de Balandougouba, les faits remontent à une mission conduite dans la localité par des agents de l'Environnement, sous la direction du directeur préfectoral. D'après ces témoignages, les présidents de districts auraient exprimé leur opposition à l'entrée de la mission dans les zones minières, par crainte de voir les équipements utilisés pour l'exploitation de l'or détruits ou endommagés. Une inquiétude liée, selon eux, aux opérations de répression menées dans la préfecture voisine de Siguiri. C'est dans ce contexte que des discussions auraient été engagées entre les responsables locaux, les Tombolamas et le maire pour trouver une issue à la situation. 105 millions GNF collectés dans plusieurs villages Dans son témoignage, notre source locale affirme que ces discussions ont abouti à une collecte d'argent auprès de plusieurs villages. Il explique que la première proposition aurait consisté à réunir 20 millions de francs guinéens par village, un montant jugé trop élevé. Après de nouvelles concertations, un compromis aurait été trouvé autour de 15 millions GNF pour les grands villages, notamment Balandougouba-centre, Kinienkoura, Faragbèkoro et Sidikila. Les villages disposant de moins d'équipements miniers auraient, quant à eux, contribué à hauteur de 5 millions GNF. « Le maire nous a demandé de faire la somme totale. Elle était de 105 millions. C'est ce que nous avons payé pour leur donner », affirme t-il Il précise que, pour les contributeurs, cet argent devait permettre aux exploitants de poursuivre leurs activités. Il ajoute qu'après cette collecte, les participants auraient reçu la consigne de garder le silence sur l'affaire. « Ils nous ont dit, comme nous avons fini de payer, de dire aux nôtres de maîtriser leurs bouches. Nous aussi, nous avons accepté cela », soutient-il. Le témoin affirme également que, malgré ces versements présumés, les activités minières auraient été sommées de s'arrêter dès le lendemain du départ de la mission. Le maire apporte sa version des faits Le maire de Balandougouba confirme l'existence de discussions entre les responsables locaux et la mission de l'Environnement. Il explique avoir convoqué les présidents de districts et les Tombolamas après avoir été informé de l'arrivée des agents, qui lui auraient annoncé une opération de répression. Selon son récit, les responsables de districts ne souhaitaient pas que les agents pénètrent dans les zones minières, redoutant notamment la destruction des machines utilisées pour l'exploitation de l'or. Le maire affirme que les discussions se sont poursuivies de 10 heures à 21 heures. Il soutient que les Tombolamas auraient ensuite été chargés de réunir de l'argent dans l'espoir d'obtenir un changement de décision. Il apporte toutefois une précision importante : selon lui, le directeur préfectoral de l'Environnement aurait initialement refusé de recevoir cette somme. « De 17 heures jusqu'à 21 heures, ils tentaient de lui donner l'argent, mais il a dit que sa personnalité ne lui permettait pas de prendre l'argent. Il a déclaré qu'il était venu pour la répression et qu'il ferait la répression le lendemain », rapporte le maire. Il affirme avoir finalement plaidé auprès du responsable de la mission, qui aurait accepté de céder sur certains points, tout en maintenant qu'il n'avait pas demandé d'argent et qu'il souhaitait effectuer sa visite de terrain. Le directeur rejette les accusations et menace de porter plainte Joint par téléphone, le directeur préfectoral de l'Environnement de Mandiana a vivement contesté les informations qui lui ont été rapportées. Rejetant toute implication dans une éventuelle perception d'argent, il a estimé que de telles accusations devaient être étayées par des preuves concrètes. Il a annoncé son intention d'engager une procédure judiciaire contre les auteurs de ces déclarations. « Pour un premier temps, il va falloir que je porte plainte […] Moi, je vais porter plainte aujourd'hui », a-t-il déclaré. Le responsable a également invité le journaliste à se rendre sur le terrain afin de vérifier les faits et de réunir les éléments justificatifs nécessaires. Au cours de cet échange, le directeur a également évoqué certaines initiatives de son service à Mandiana, notamment des activités de reboisement et une cérémonie organisée à l'occasion de la Journée mondiale des éléphants. Il a regretté, selon ses propos, que les actions positives de son service ne bénéficient pas de la même attention que les accusations portées contre lui. Plusieurs questions restent sans réponse Au-delà de ces déclarations contradictoires, plusieurs interrogations demeurent : les 105 millions de francs guinéens ont-ils effectivement été collectés et remis ? Qui en aurait été le véritable destinataire ? La mission de l'Environnement a-t-elle finalement renoncé à certaines opérations de contrôle à la suite des discussions ? Pour l'heure, les témoignages recueillis constituent des accusations qui restent à vérifier. De son côté, le directeur préfectoral de l'Environnement conteste les faits qui lui sont imputés et réclame des preuves. À Mandiana, cette affaire relance le débat sur le contrôle des activités minières, la protection de l'environnement et les conditions d'application des mesures de répression dans les zones d'exploitation aurifère de Balandougouba. Karifa Doumbouya, correspondant régional – Kankan L’article Mandiana : le directeur préfectoral de l'Environnement accusé d'avoir perçu 105 millions GNF pour renoncer à un contrôle minier est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: KP plans to set up faceless ATCs, spend Rs70bn on CTD and police in a year as part of counterterrorism initiatives
items.description: The administrative setup in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa plans to establish faceless anti-terrorism courts in the province as part of its initiatives to strengthen the fight against terrorism, according to a briefing by the officials televised on Sunday. KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi was also present at the briefing, where KP Secretary Home Amjad Ali Khan outlined several measures planned to step up the fight against terrorism and explained that witnesses in terrorism cases feared coming forward. “So, we have recently sent the amendment to set up faceless anti-terrorism courts. Through this, not just the protection of witnesses, but that of prosecutors and judges will also be ensured,” he said. Moreover, he said the administrative setup planned to spend Rs70 billion on the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) and police in a year, in order to increase their capacity. Talking about dealing with terrorism in the policy domain, Khan noted that in the past there had been a “lack of political ownership” in the fight against terrorism in the province. “Our armed forces and law enforcement agencies are making sacrifices in the war against terrorism; however, [..] the provincial government was not taking ownership for them.” The Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP on Oct 11, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. Khan stressed the need for a “close liaison” on terrorism between the public, political leadership, and security forces. He further recalled that despite the Centre formulating an Afghan policy, “actions continued to be taken in the province contrary to that policy, leading to confusion among the people”. He also noted that there was “propaganda against the security forces in attempts to sabotage the counterterrorism efforts in the province”. The official then spoke of the “insufficient funding” for civil law enforcement agencies (LEAs), including police and CTD, particularly in the merged districts, where he said only 3.2 per cent of the budget was allocated for security. He highlighted a shortage of over 10,000 personnel in the police, while also noting the lack of security infrastructure. “Along with that, in the merged districts, most of the dependence regarding the police force is on former ex-Fata Khasadars and Levies,” he said, adding that the police personnel did not receive adequate training. He further highlighted inadequate counter-drone protection, for which the available system was at a capacity of 12pc, noting that terrorists were using drone technology as well, “due to which we are suffering considerable losses”. He also highlighted the lack of adequate Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) teams. “Because of these issues [..] we have suffered significant losses over the past two or three years in which 1,003 personnel of the armed forces were martyred, 627 police personnel, and 808 civilian casualties occurred,” he stated. Referring to the Centre’s Rs160bn package for uplift of KP, Khan said that the provincial set-up and the federal government were on the same page, expressing hope that “its effects will be seen in the coming days”. He went on to outline plans to strengthen police capacity in the province, including fortifying sensitive police stations and check posts, extending the Safe City project, and establishing anti-drone systems in Dera Ismail Khan, Lakki Marwat, and Bannu as well as functionalising District Nerve Centres in ten districts. Updated information will be available to LEAs from the centres, he added. Under the legal interventions in policing, the official said that faceless ATC courts will be set up. “Witnesses in terrorism cases are afraid to come forward due to their identity. So we have recently sent the amendment for these faceless courts. Through this measure, witnesses, prosecutors, and judges will have their protection ensured,” he stated. Detailing the technical abilities of the police, the official said that satellite communication systems were being set up in areas with no prior communication system. He added that the provincial administration was also deploying AI tools for social media monitoring to counter terrorists’ narrative. Khan also stressed the need for increased public outreach, including strengthening District Dispute Resolution Councils as well as establishing tribal liaison committees. “Regular jirgas will be held with notables, regular interaction will occur with the public, and community mobilisation will take place,” he stated. He also outlined plans for police to be trained in modern technology such as anti-drone systems and sniping. He also recalled the provincial setup’s decision to revise packages for martyred police personnel. Khan continued: “Kinetic operations will be scaled up so that militancy can be eliminated. In this regard, intelligence-based operations will be enhanced, area sanitisation will be carried out [..], terrorist facilitators will be arrested, and re-verification will also be carried out for people on the fourth schedule to ensure none of them is providing facilitation or support to terrorists. He also added that the Rapid Response Force will be mobilised. Khan added that the provincial administration also planned to increase the number of police check posts. He announced that the government was spending Rs70bn on CTD and police annually. “In this regard, the police are being given Rs59.8bn, of which Rs33.4bn will be for their infrastructure and Rs26.4bn will be for procurement, while Rs10.3bn is being given to the CTD, of which Rs5.4bn is for infrastructure, and Rs4.9bn for procurement.” He added that police surveillance capacity — at 15pc presently — will be increased to 60pc, while for CTD it will be enhanced by 70pc. “The police’s counter-aerial threat capacity, which is currently at 1pc, will be taken up to 50pc. Our air strike capability is currently at 18pc and will be increased to 50pc, as well as night fighting capacity, with vehicle armour capacity of the police to be improved by 45pc,” the official said. He added that “jammer availability was at 40pc but will be increased to 50pc while counter-drone capability — at 52pc presently — will be increased to 60pc”. Protective gear and vehicle availability will be improved as well, while specialised training will be held in collaboration with the Pakistan Armed Forces. The official also announced action against smuggling, narcotics, extortion and non-custom-paid vehicles. “The purpose of all these measures is to provide a safe and secure environment to the people of KP where they can spend their lives, according to their codes and traditions,” Khan concluded. Since the imposition of the governor’s rule in KP, the provincial administration has vowed to steer the province towards development and eliminate terrorism. Chairing his first apex committee meeting after taking charge of the province, governor Kundi promised to equip police and CTD with resources. “Whatever weapons you want, whatever you need, we will get them to you. We will not compromise on our police officers and personnel. We will equip them well,” Kundi had said at the meeting. Last month, he also announced an increase in the compensation packages for police officers martyred or injured in the line of duty. Governor Kundi calls for ownership of war against terrorism Speaking at the occasion, Governor Kundi said the provincial government’s priority was to restore peace and strengthen the police force, stressing that development would follow once security was ensured. He said the police were at the forefront of the war against terrorism and needed to be adequately equipped to carry out their responsibilities. “Until we strengthen and facilitate [the police], how will they fight using just one Kalashnikov and a few bullets?” Kundi asked. While the government had announced compensation packages for the families of police martyrs and was working on improving police salaries, it would also provide the force with weapons, ammunition and other resources, Kundi stressed during his speech. “We talk a lot about merged districts, but as far as I know, not a single police line has been created in our merged districts, our former Fata. Look at their police stations, check posts, and facilities,” Kundi highlighted, adding that the government had directed the chief secretary and additional chief secretary to prepare a comprehensive package in this regard. He said the plan also included solarising and equipping police facilities. The governor pointed out the “lack of political ownership” previously with regard to the war against terrorism in the province. “When something happened here, voices always came from the assemblies saying that this is ‘not our war’. We don’t own it,” Kundi said. He questioned what the families of martyrs would say when political leaders did not take ownership of the war. “For whom did the martyr make this sacrifice? Was it for this soil, this country, or was it made under a specific agenda?” he asserted. “If I have a gunman who is there for my protection, and I say that I don’t even own this gunman, how will he protect me?” Kundi asked rhetorically. According to the governor, not owning the war indicated a lack of coordination. Kundi referred to the security situation in parts of KP, adding that political leaders, including a former chief minister and JUI-F’s Maulana Fazlur Rehman, had acknowledged difficulties in moving freely in certain areas. “If intelligence-based operations do not take place and the police and security forces do not conduct operations, how will these problems be resolved?” he asked. Kundi said the current set-up’s stance was “clear” and that decisions and policies would be made in Islamabad rather than “Kabul, Kandahar or Jalalabad”. The governor alleged that Afghanistan was facilitating India and Israel in using its territory against Pakistan. He referred to reports of drones entering Pakistan, saying some had crossed the border but were intercepted by Pakistani forces. He then criticised the lack of response by the previous government to statements by Afghan ministers threatening to take over Peshawar. Kundi said Pakistan had repeatedly raised its concerns about Afghan soil being used to facilitate terrorism at international forums through the Foreign Office and the deputy prime minister and foreign minister, but Kabul had not budged an inch on addressing the issue. “It is very clear that whoever does not accept our state, Constitution and laws cannot be engaged in dialogue. Anyone who takes up arms against the state cannot be offered dialogue; they will be responded to accordingly,” Kundi asserted. During his speech, the governor stressed the importance of winning public trust, recalling that the province began its journey towards peace in 2008, when it was grappling with suicide bombings, target killings, kidnappings for ransom, among other problems. He said public support had been crucial to previous military operations and would remain essential to counterterrorism efforts. “You saw we cleared Swat; the world’s largest displacement occurred at that time, and we rehabilitated the people. People supported us for the operation.” Reiterating that the government had a zero-tolerance policy towards terrorism, Kundi said the fight against it remained its foremost priority, with development coming afterwards. “You can build roads, large underpasses and even turn the city into a garden, but what is the point if the people themselves are not safe?” he said. He stressed that people needed to be assured that their children could go to school, college and playgrounds and return safely, while family members could travel to work or conduct business without fear. The governor also called for greater engagement of the province’s large youth population through “positive activities”.

items.title: Guinée : Baowu Resources expose les avantages du projet Simandou
items.description: Selon un communiqué de Baowu Resources parvenu à notre rédaction, l’entreprise chinoise a publié, le 6 novembre à Shanghai, en marge de la neuvième Exposition internationale d’importation de Chine (CIIE), un rapport thématique ESG consacré à la durabilité du projet minier de Simandou, en Guinée. La cérémonie s’est déroulée en présence du ministre guinéen de l’Environnement et du Développement durable, Fassou Théa. Au cours de cette cérémonie, celui-ci a souligné que « le projet Simandou était aujourd'hui bien plus qu'un projet minier. Il marque une transformation historique pour l'économie guinéenne et offre une opportunité exceptionnelle de création d’emplois, de développement des infrastructures et d'amélioration des conditions de vie des populations guinéennes », rapporte le communiqué. Le président de Baowu Resources, Cao Zhifu, a pour sa part réaffirmé l’engagement de l’entreprise à accompagner les différentes parties prenantes. Il a déclaré que « Baowu Resources était disposé à travailler avec toutes les parties pour faire progresser le développement durable de Simandou de manière plus stable, plus concrète et plus ambitieuse », indique la même source. Présenté comme le premier document public ESG consacré à Simandou, le rapport expose une démarche fondée sur le partenariat, le progrès et la prospérité, associant développement minier, protection de l’environnement et renforcement des capacités locales. L’ambition affichée est de faire bénéficier les populations guinéennes et les partenaires du projet des retombées de son développement, précise le texte.

items.title: Vote-buying won’t work in 2027, APM candidate tells Ondo voters
items.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Allied Peoples Movement (APM) senatorial candidate for Ondo Central, Hon. Sunday Falae, has urged voters in Ondo State to reject vote-buying and vote according to their conscience in the 2027 general elections. Falae, who spoke in an interview in Akure, said financial inducements would not determine voters’ choices in the forthcoming elections, claiming that many Nigerians were dissatisfied with the state of affairs and wanted a change. “They can bring all the money they want, it is not going to work. I am on the streets every day and the anger is there. Look at what happened in Osun,” he said. He described what he called a “Rainbow Coalition”, a voting pattern in which individuals support candidates from different political parties for various elective positions rather than voting exclusively for one party. Falae illustrated the trend with the example of a woman who reportedly told him she intended to vote for the APC presidential candidate, him for Senate, an ADC candidate for the House of Representatives and an SDP candidate for the State House of Assembly. “People are angry and they want change. They will take the money and vote their conscience,” he said. On the management of public funds, the APM candidate questioned the accountability of state governors over increased allocations, arguing that the funds received by state governments were not reflected in the level of development across the country. “We are not holding them responsible. The amount of money they are getting does not correspond to the development we are seeing,” he said. He cited the Owena-Alade-Idanre road, which he alleged was awarded and paid for but remained unconstructed. “That road should have been constructed. That money today, we don’t know where it is. The road was not constructed and it was approved and paid. So the money went to somebody’s pocket,” he alleged. Falae argued that accountability should not be limited to the Federal Government, saying state governors, senators and local government chairmen must also explain how public funds allocated to their respective jurisdictions were spent. On the 2027 presidential election, he said the South-West should complete its eight-year presidential tenure, arguing that the contest should be between President Bola Tinubu of the APC and Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, whom he identified as the APM’s presidential candidate. He explained that he did not join the African Democratic Congress because he did not want to campaign against Tinubu. “In all sincerity, I didn’t join the ADC because I didn’t want to campaign against the President. I want us as Yorubas to finish eight years in office. Buhari finished his eight years,” he said. Falae said he eventually joined the APM because Makinde, whom he described as a fellow Yoruba, could complete the remaining four years of the South-West’s presidential tenure. “Tinubu deserves a second term. But if you give it to Governor Makinde, that is fine. Does he deserve it? Yes. Does Makinde deserve it? Even better. He has the energy and he has done well in Oyo State,” he said. He also praised Makinde’s performance in Oyo State, arguing that his administration demonstrated the kind of leadership he believed Nigeria needed. Explaining his decision to contest the Ondo Central senatorial seat, Falae said the district had been inadequately represented over the past four years. He disclosed that he was a member of the APC from its formation until April 2026, but left the party over what he described as inadequate representation of the constituency. “I am interested because I am under-represented right now. I was in the APC from inception until April this year. The person we have there now is not representing us the way he should. I have been to all six local governments and everybody is complaining,” he said. Falae added that constituents felt abandoned and believed there was little to show for the outgoing tenure of their current representative. items.title: Anglican Church warns Tinubu, INEC against 2027 election manipulation
items.description: By Chimaobi Nwaiwu NNEWI — The Church of Nigeria (Anglican Communion), Province of the Niger, has warned the Presidency, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) against manipulating the 2027 general elections or taking Nigerians for granted. The church also cautioned against moves towards a one-party system, describing the alleged intimidation of opposition parties and their candidates as dangerous to the country’s democracy. It urged Nigerians not to approach the 2027 presidential and other elections with indifference but to use their votes to hold political leaders accountable for unfulfilled promises. The Coordinating Bishop of the Province of the Niger, Bishop of Aguata and Supervising Bishop of the Diocese of Awka, Rt. Rev. Dr Samuel C. Ezeofor, gave the warning during the 2026 Anglican Prayer Rally of Anambra State (APRAS). Ezeofor recalled that the province had, during its synod in May, warned Nigerians about the dangers of a one-party system and urged citizens to remain vigilant. He said, “This is the time for us to come out to show that we are human beings, that we are not robots and so everywhere in the country, we are calling upon Nigerians to take their future, and destiny in their hands with the forthcoming presidential and other elections in the country.” Addressing the Presidency, INEC, the APC and other political stakeholders, the bishop said Nigerians were increasingly dissatisfied with developments in the country and should not be taken for granted. “If they take Nigerians for granted, it may come to a point where there may be a revolution. I don’t pray for that, but by my training, I am trained to believe the best but be prepared for the worst,” he said. He urged those involved in the 2027 electoral process to respect the wishes of voters and ensure that the outcome reflected their choices. “So both the Presidency, APC, INEC and all the people who are involved in the election that is coming in 2027, let everyone of them be careful and do what Nigerians said with their ballots and would want to be done with their votes,” he added. On the internal challenges facing the Province of the Niger, Ezeofor acknowledged that some Anglican faithful might have become discouraged by the crisis within the church. He, however, urged them to remain steadfast, saying that setbacks in the church’s human administration did not mean God had abandoned it. “My message to our faithfuls is that as human beings, we may stumble, but God is still on his throne. This church belongs to God, yet it is human beings who run the church and it is also a human system,” he said. He encouraged members to continue looking up to Jesus Christ, whom he described as the author and finisher of their faith, expressing optimism that the situation would improve. The 2026 prayer rally, themed “Dwelling in the Secret Place of the Most High God”, was attended by six bishops of the province, including the retired Archbishop of the Province of the Niger, Most Rev. Prof. Godwin Okpara. Others in attendance were Bishop Ephraim Ikeako of the Diocese of Amichi, Bishop Prosper Amah of the Diocese of Ogbaru, Bishop Ndubuisi Obi of the Diocese of Nnewi and Bishop Obiora Uzochukwu of the Diocese of Niger East. Earlier, the preacher at the rally, Venerable Dr Emma Ezeugo, urged Christians to devote more time to prayer and fasting, particularly as December approaches. He said prayer brought peace, protection and peace of mind, urging believers to seek God’s presence in their daily lives. items.title: PM Shehbaz, Nawaz discuss ‘matters of national importance’ as Sharifs gather at Lahore's Jati Umra
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif discussed matters of “national importance” with PML-N President Nawaz Sharif during a visit to the latter’s residence in Lahore’s Jati Umra on Sunday, state-run Radio Pakistan reported . The outlet reported that the two leaders held detailed discussions regarding the country’s political situation as well as “other matters of national importance”. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and Nawaz’s daughter, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, were also present on the occasion. PM Shehbaz briefed the PML-N president on the law and order situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and on recent initiatives taken for the development and prosperity of the province, Radio Pakistan added. The Centre has imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP since Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism, and the new administrative setup led by Governor Faisal Karim Kundi has stressed that improving counterterrorism measures is its topmost priority. Both PM Shehbaz and his brother Nawaz have defended the decision to impose the emergency, with the premier saying the federal government had been “compel­led” to take the step over security conce­rns and the elder Sharif arguing that the intervention should have come much earlier. The premier also apprised Nawaz of “the ongoing economic reforms by the government, the challenges being faced and the measures being taken to address them”, the outlet said. The meeting also deliberated on ways to improve the national economy further, it added.

items.description: El presidente del Gobierno y candidato socialista a la reelección, Pedro Sánchez, se ha comprometido este domingo a blindar en la Constitución la revalorización de las pensiones conforme al IPC en la próxima legislatura. “Se lo vamos a exigir a todos los grupos parlamentarios, para que nadie vuelva a jugar con el futuro de las pensiones”, ha aseverado en un mitin ante 2.800 militantes y simpatizantes en Bilbao. Mientras, el líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, se ha desplazado a Málaga junto al presidente andaluz, Juan Manuel Moreno. items.title: Profession d’avocat : les textes d’application attendus avant la fin de l’année
items.description: La réforme de la profession d’avocat entre dans une nouvelle phase. Le ministre de la Justice, Abdellatif Ouahbi, a annoncé que plusieurs textes d’application de la loi n° 66.23 relative à l’organisation de la profession étaient prêts, notamment ceux concernant la formation et la création d’un institut dédié. Leur adoption devrait être engagée prochainement au Conseil de gouvernement, avec une finalisation prévue avant la fin de l’année. Dans une déclaration à Hespress , le ministre a précisé que les travaux se poursuivaient pour élaborer les autres textes réglementaires nécessaires à la mise en œuvre de la loi. Ces démarches se déroulent toutefois sans concertation avec l’Association des barreaux du Maroc (ABAM), qui continue de boycotter le dialogue avec le ministère de la Justice. Pour Abdellatif Ouahbi, les tensions ont désormais dépassé leur stade initial et la situation appelle à passer à l’application effective de la loi. Le ministre a, par ailleurs, écarté l’hypothèse d’une modification du texte, malgré les réserves persistantes qu’il suscite. Adoptée à la fin du précédent mandat gouvernemental, la loi n’a pas encore été appliquée dans des conditions permettant, selon lui, d’envisager sa révision. Le ministère entend donc poursuivre son travail de mise en œuvre et préparer les textes d’application prévus par le législateur. Cette position intervient alors que le Parti de l’Istiqlal a évoqué la possibilité de remettre le texte en discussion. Son président du Conseil national, Abdeljebbar Rachidi, avait notamment exprimé cette option lors d’un entretien avec Hespress . En réponse, le ministre a souligné que la volonté d’une composante de la majorité gouvernementale de modifier la loi ne signifiait pas nécessairement que cette proposition serait concrétisée. Il a rappelé que le texte avait achevé son parcours législatif et qu’un dahir chérifien portant son exécution avait été publié. Cinq instituts de formation envisagés Au-delà des enjeux politiques et institutionnels, la réforme prévoit une nouvelle organisation de la formation des avocats. Lors d’une réunion de la commission de la justice, de la législation et des droits de l’homme à la Chambre des représentants, au cours de la semaine, Abdellatif Ouahbi a évoqué un dispositif à vocation quasi régionale. Cinq villes devraient ainsi accueillir des instituts de formation : Oujda, Agadir, Marrakech, Casablanca et Tétouan. À Casablanca, un ancien établissement scolaire a été mis à la disposition du ministère de la Justice, qui prévoit de le transformer en institut dédié à la profession d’avocat. Une autre structure, située à Tétouan, a également été confiée au département, qui compte l’aménager à cette même fin. Ces établissements devraient permettre la création de plusieurs instituts, chacun accueillant entre 50 et 70 avocats stagiaires. La formation s’étendrait sur une année et associerait enseignements théoriques et stages pratiques. Le ministre a présenté ces éléments comme constituant le cadre général du futur dispositif. Un examen d’accès dans au moins deux langues La réforme concerne également les modalités d’accès aux professions juridiques. Abdellatif Ouahbi a affirmé que l’examen d’entrée dans les professions de notaire et d’avocat serait soumis à des exigences particulièrement strictes. Les candidats devront notamment passer les épreuves dans au moins deux langues. La maîtrise d’une seule langue ne sera donc pas suffisante pour accéder à ces professions. The post Profession d’avocat : les textes d’application attendus avant la fin de l’année appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: MIC : Guinée–Türkiye, l’agro-industrie et les investissements au cœur de la mission
items.description: Transformer les ressources en Guinée, développer les partenariats industriels et ouvrir de nouvelles perspectives commerciales : ces priorités ont guidé les échanges du Ministre de l’Industrie et du Commerce, Monsieur Aboubacar KOUROUMA, au cours de sa mission en Türkiye. Le mardi 3 novembre 2026, au cours du forum africain « Agriconnect », une rencontres avec les milieux d’affaires turcs, la délégation guinéenne a présenté les ambitions économiques du pays et exploré les possibilités de les traduire en projets concrets. Faire de la transformation agricole un moteur de croissance Consacré au partage d’expériences et à l’identification d’opportunités dans l’agriculture et la transformation agricole, le forum Agriconnect a réuni plusieurs délégations africaines, en présence notamment des ministres du Commerce de Türkiye et du Sénégal. À cette occasion, le Ministre Aboubacar KOUROUMA a mis en avant la dimension inclusive et panafricaine du Programme de développement socioéconomique durable et responsable Simandou 2040. Il a défendu une ambition : permettre à l’Afrique de prendre pleinement sa place dans les chaînes de valeur mondiales en développant ses propres capacités de production et de transformation. « L’Afrique tient dorénavant à transformer ses ressources sur place », a-t-il affirmé. Au-delà du potentiel minier guinéen, le Ministre a rappelé la volonté du Gouvernement de faire de l’agriculture un véritable moteur de l’économie. La valorisation des terres agricoles et le développement de la transformation locale constituent, à ce titre, des leviers pour créer davantage de valeur et d’emplois en Guinée. Renforcer les échanges avec les entreprises turques La délégation a ensuite rencontré des représentants du MÜSİAD, une organisation patronale turque réunissant notamment des entreprises industrielles et commerciales. Les discussions avec les investisseurs, issus entre autres des secteurs de la construction et du commerce, ont porté sur le renforcement des relations économiques entre les deux pays. Les parties ont réaffirmé leur volonté d’intensifier leurs efforts pour atteindre l’objectif commun de 500 millions de dollars d’échanges économiques et commerciaux. Avec Albayrak, avancer vers des projets concrets En fin de journée, le Ministre et sa délégation ont été reçus par Monsieur Ahmet Albayrak, Président du Conseil d’administration du groupe Albayrak. Après une présentation du parcours du groupe, les échanges ont permis de faire le point sur ses activités en Guinée et d’examiner ses perspectives de développement à court, moyen et long terme. Le Ministre a invité le groupe à renforcer sa participation à l’industrialisation du pays, particulièrement dans la transformation agricole. Les deux parties sont convenues de poursuivre rapidement les discussions afin de faire émerger des projets concrets, susceptibles d’être mis en œuvre dans les meilleurs délais et bénéfiques aux deux pays. items.title: Hashim raises alarm over 3.68m IDPs, insecurity before US commission
items.description: ABUJA — Accord Party presidential candidate, Dr Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has drawn the attention of the United States Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) to Nigeria’s estimated 3.68 million internally displaced persons (IDPs), calling for greater international intervention over insecurity, religious persecution and ethnic discrimination. Hashim also called for the release of Hausa cultural activist, Maisango, whom he alleged was being unlawfully detained, and urged the international community to investigate reports of attacks and the burning of 11 villages in Shanga Local Government Area of Kebbi State. He made the appeal during an engagement with the commission on Friday, where he discussed Nigeria’s religious freedom and humanitarian challenges. According to a statement on the engagement, Hashim acknowledged that Christians in Northern Nigeria face persecution but argued that religious freedom violations also affect Muslim minorities, including Shia Muslims and Hausa communities. He said Nigeria’s religious freedom challenges extended beyond the conventional Christian-Muslim divide, alleging that ethnic identity and cultural affiliation also influenced religious and social acceptance in some communities. The Accord candidate particularly raised concerns about what he described as the marginalisation of Hausa Muslims in parts of Northern Nigeria, arguing that some communities experience unequal treatment despite sharing the same Islamic faith with other groups. On Maisango’s detention, Hashim alleged that the cultural activist had been held without trial despite reportedly being dismissed from his employment with the Department of State Services (DSS). He called for his immediate release, emphasising the need to respect due process and fundamental human rights. Hashim also cited an estimated 3.68 million internally displaced persons in Nigeria, referencing UNHCR figures as of October 2026, and argued that the humanitarian crisis cut across religious and ethnic boundaries. He specifically highlighted reported attacks on communities in Shanga Local Government Area of Kebbi State, including Kalkami, Tungar Bori and Kawara. According to him, reports of attacks in April 2026 indicated that suspected bandits killed residents, set buildings ablaze and forced inhabitants to flee their homes. He said reports that 11 villages were burnt in the area deserved sustained international attention. Hashim further alleged that some armed groups operating in the region were more interested in killing residents, destroying settlements and taking control of territory than in religious conversion. He blamed what he described as the government’s failure to adequately protect vulnerable communities and decisively confront armed groups, warning that the country’s security and religious freedom challenges must not deteriorate further ahead of another political transition. The presidential candidate also criticised what he termed insufficient accountability under the present administration, alleging that political considerations had weakened efforts to tackle terrorism and other forms of armed violence. He recalled that the United States designated Nigeria a Country of Particular Concern in October 2025 over religious freedom concerns, following earlier recommendations by USCIRF. He said the international community should recognise victims of religious and ethnic persecution across all communities rather than concentrate on one religious group. Hashim called for a comprehensive approach that addresses the experiences of Christians, Shia Muslims, Hausa communities and other vulnerable populations, while ensuring that state institutions protect constitutionally guaranteed rights. He commended the commission for its work on religious freedom in Nigeria and acknowledged US President Donald Trump’s interest in the issue. He said religious freedom was “an intrinsic part of democratic right”. The post Hashim raises alarm over 3.68m IDPs, insecurity before US commission appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le Cercle Sénégal-Maroc d’amitié et de fraternité dévoile ses ambitions au khalife général des mourides
items.description: Le Cercle Sénégal-Maroc d’amitié et de fraternité (CESEMAF) poursuit ses efforts en faveur du rapprochement entre les deux peuples. Une délégation de l’organisation, conduite par son président, Amadou Kane, a été reçue, samedi 7 novembre, par le khalife général des mourides, Serigne Mountakha Mbacké à Touba . Cette audience a permis aux responsables de présenter leur plan d’action ainsi que leurs initiatives dans les domaines social et éducatif. Au cours des échanges, le président du CESEMAF a annoncé plusieurs projets destinés à soutenir les communautés des huit anciens villages de reclassement social. Parmi les initiatives envisagées figure la mise en place d’activités productives, notamment la création d’une unité de transformation des déchets plastiques dans l’un de ces villages, situé dans la région de Kolda. Le projet vise à valoriser ces déchets en produits commercialisables et à générer des revenus pour les populations locales, particulièrement les femmes. L’organisation a également fait part de sa volonté de contribuer à la réhabilitation de la Maison du Sénégal au Maroc, notamment à Fès. Cette résidence, dont l’état de dégradation a été signalé par des dignitaires religieux, devrait bénéficier d’un programme de restauration avec l’appui des partenaires du CESEMAF. Sur le volet éducatif, onze bourses d’études, dont une entière et dix demi-bourses, ont été mises à la disposition du guide religieux. Une démarche qui traduit l’engagement de l’organisation en faveur de la formation des jeunes. À l’issue de l’audience, la délégation a sollicité les prières de Serigne Mountakha Mbacké pour la consolidation des relations d’amitié et de fraternité entre le Sénégal et le Maroc. Le secrétaire général du CESEMAF, Lahlou Sidi Mouhamed, a, pour sa part, invité les jeunes à la vigilance face à certains médias étrangers qui, selon lui, diffusent des contenus susceptibles de fragiliser les relations entre les deux peuples. Birane DIOP (correspondant)

items.title: Bandits kill 12 family members, abduct others in Zamfara
items.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Armed men suspected to be bandits have killed 12 members of the same family and abducted several residents during an attack on Gidan Taba village in Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara State. The attack reportedly occurred on Saturday night in Dosara Birnin Kaya Ward, with the assailants setting a room ablaze after the family members reportedly locked themselves inside to avoid being abducted. A source in the area told Vanguard that the victims belonged to the family of one Mallam Muhammadu Sani, who had gathered his relatives in a single room in an attempt to protect them from the attackers. According to the source, the bandits ordered the occupants to open the door but, after they refused, set fire around the room, killing all 12 family members. Several other residents were also reportedly abducted during the raid, although the exact number of those kidnapped could not be immediately ascertained. The 12 victims were buried on Sunday morning in accordance with Islamic rites. The attack comes amid recurring bandit attacks and security concerns along the busy Gusau-Sokoto road, where commuters have continued to face threats from armed criminals. Residents condemned the killings, describing the incident as barbaric, and called on security agencies and the Zamfara State Government to intensify efforts to protect lives and property. As of the time of filing this report, security agencies had yet to issue an official statement on the attack. The post Bandits kill 12 family members, abduct others in Zamfara appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Hamza Zahoor’s unbeaten century guides Pakistan U-19 to thrilling win over India
items.description: Hamza Zahoor produced a match-winning unbeaten century as Pakistan Under-19 defeated arch-rivals India by three wickets in a thrilling Group ‘A’ encounter of the ACC Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Muscat on Sunday. Chasing 209, Pakistan reached the target in 48.1 overs, finishing on 211 for seven, with Hamza holding his nerve under pressure to steer his side home. The wicket-keeper-batter remained unbeaten on 100 off 108 balls, striking 10 fours and three sixes, and was named Player of the Match. Pakistan’s chase, however, was far from straightforward as India’s bowlers made early inroads to reduce them to 61 for five. Hamza then joined Hasnain Abbas Dar, who contributed 38, to revive the innings with a crucial partnership. With wickets falling at the other end, Hamza showed remarkable composure, combining caution with timely aggression to keep Pakistan on course. He eventually guided the lower order across the finish line with 11 balls to spare, completing a memorable century in the process. Earlier, India, after electing to bat, were bowled out for 208 in 46.3 overs. Their innings got off to a disastrous start when captain and opener Lakshya Rajesh Raichandani was dismissed for a duck off the second ball. India slipped further to 22 for three, leaving their middle order under considerable pressure. Arjun Rajput then mounted a spirited recovery with an outstanding 107 off 85 deliveries, hitting 11 fours and five sixes. However, the right-hander received little support from the other end as Pakistan’s bowlers maintained pressure and regularly picked up wickets to restrict India to a modest total. Ali Raza, Rizwanullah and Niqab Shafiq shared the spoils with three wickets apiece, while Mohammad Sayyam claimed one. The victory takes Pakistan to the top of Group ‘A’ with four points from two matches, having registered back-to-back wins. India, meanwhile, have two points from as many games, with one victory and one defeat. Both teams have one group fixture remaining, with the top two sides advancing to the semi-finals.

items.title: Court awards N50m damages against Pararan over defamation
items.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi EFFURUN — A Delta State High Court sitting in Effurun, Uvwie Local Government Area, has awarded N50 million in damages against the proprietor of Pararan Mock News, Diamond Dietanuru Osakorigho, popularly known as Pararan, over a Facebook publication found to be defamatory against Apostle Michael Akpor. The court, presided over by Justice R.D. Harriman, also ordered Osakorigho to publish an unreserved apology to the cleric in Vanguard and The Nation newspapers within 14 days. It directed that the apology must enjoy the same prominence and circulation as the original publication. The judgment was delivered on November 6, 2026, in Suit No. EHC/91/2023. The court further restrained the defendant, his agents, privies, servants and all persons acting through him from publishing or causing to be published any further defamatory, injurious or libellous statements, videos or other materials against Akpor. It also awarded N1 million as costs of the suit. The case arose from a Facebook publication made on July 20, 2022, with the caption, “Warri Pastor Kpuf 2Keke passenger”, which the court found to be false and defamatory. Reacting to the judgment, counsel to the cleric, Austin Nyekigbe, a human rights activist, described the ruling as a significant statement on responsible social media engagement. He said the judgment reinforced the principle that freedom to use social media did not confer the right to publish false and defamatory information about others. “People must learn to verify information before rushing to publish it, particularly on social media. An injustice to one is an injustice to all,” he said. Also commenting on the judgment, a Warri-based lawyer, Mrs Eloho Avwaruroro-Okoye, who was present in court, said the decision underscored the legal consequences of irresponsible online publications. According to her, freedom of expression comes with responsibility, adding that those who publish false and damaging information must be prepared to face the legal consequences. She congratulated Akpor on his victory and commended Nyekigbe for his diligence in handling the case. The legal dispute followed allegations linking Akpor and two policemen attached to him to the July 12, 2022, killing of two persons at Ugbolokposo community in Effurun. However, Nyekigbe said police investigations subsequently exonerated his client and the two officers, identified as ASP Mesoro Victor and Inspector Ignatius Achazie. He said findings from the investigation, including witness statements, vehicle identification exercises and church CCTV footage, contradicted allegations linking the cleric to the killings. According to him, the police investigation report established that Akpor was at his church when the incident occurred, concluding that he was “going on with his religious business in the Church”. Nyekigbe, however, expressed sympathy with the families of the deceased. The post Court awards N50m damages against Pararan over defamation appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Assemblée nationale : Mamadou Bhoye Bah remercie Mamadi Doumbouya pour le déclassement de Wanindara et plaide pour le développement de Sonfonia
items.description: À l’occasion d’une séance plénière de l’Assemblée nationale, l’Honorable Mamadou Bhoye Bah, député de la commune de Sonfonia, a pris la parole pour porter les préoccupations de ses concitoyens et exprimer sa reconnaissance au Président de la République, le Général Mamadi Doumbouya, pour la décision relative au déclassement de la zone de Wanindara. Dans son intervention, le parlementaire a mis en évidence la portée sociale et symbolique de cette décision, qui représente une nouvelle perspective pour de nombreuses familles longtemps confrontées à des difficultés liées à leur situation foncière. Au-delà de cette mesure, il s'agit d'une opportunité de renforcer la sécurité des habitations, de favoriser les activités économiques et d'améliorer les conditions de vie des populations concernées. WANINDARA : UN ESPOIR POUR LES FAMILLES, LES FEMMES ET LES ACTEURS ÉCONOMIQUES Cette décision revêt une importance particulière pour les femmes, notamment les commerçantes et les nombreuses mamans qui contribuent quotidiennement à la vie économique de la commune. La sécurisation de leurs espaces de vie et d'activité constitue un enjeu essentiel pour leur permettre de développer leurs commerces, de renforcer leur autonomie économique et de participer davantage au développement local. Pour l'Honorable Mamadou Bhoye Bah, les décisions publiques doivent avant tout produire des effets concrets dans la vie des citoyens, particulièrement ceux qui attendent depuis longtemps des réponses à leurs préoccupations. SONFONIA, UNE COMMUNE STRATÉGIQUE QUI MÉRITE DAVANTAGE D'INVESTISSEMENTS Au-delà du dossier de Wanindara, cette prise de parole permet de replacer Sonfonia au cœur des réflexions sur le développement urbain et économique de la capitale. Commune à fort potentiel démographique, économique et humain, Sonfonia dispose d'atouts importants qui méritent d'être davantage valorisés. Sa jeunesse dynamique, ses femmes entrepreneures, ses acteurs économiques et ses nombreuses initiatives communautaires constituent un capital humain précieux pour l'avenir de la Guinée. À cet effet, plusieurs priorités méritent une attention particulière : le renforcement des infrastructures routières, la construction et la réhabilitation des établissements scolaires, l'amélioration des structures sanitaires, l'aménagement des marchés, la réalisation d'espaces sportifs et culturels, ainsi que le développement d'infrastructures modernes adaptées à l'évolution de la commune. La jeunesse de Sonfonia, particulièrement engagée dans les initiatives citoyennes, sociales et communautaires, doit également bénéficier de davantage d'espaces d'expression, de formation, d'encadrement et d'opportunités d’emploi. Les jeunes qui œuvrent pour la paix, la cohésion sociale et le vivre-ensemble représentent une force importante qu'il convient d'accompagner et de responsabiliser. Dans cette même dynamique, les femmes et les mamans de Sonfonia doivent occuper une place centrale dans les politiques de développement. Leur participation à la vie économique et sociale mérite d'être soutenue par des initiatives favorisant l'entrepreneuriat, la formation professionnelle et l'accès aux opportunités. UN APPEL AUX INVESTISSEURS ET AUX PARTENAIRES AU DÉVELOPPEMENT Compte tenu de ses potentialités, Sonfonia mérite également de retenir l'attention des investisseurs nationaux et internationaux. La commune offre des perspectives dans plusieurs secteurs, notamment le commerce, l'immobilier, les services, l'éducation, la santé, les infrastructures et les activités génératrices d’emplois. L'Honorable Mamadou Bhoye Bah entend ainsi placer les enjeux du développement local parmi les préoccupations qui doivent être davantage portées au sein des institutions de la République. Sonfonia est également une commune où la paix, la cohésion sociale et la solidarité communautaire constituent des valeurs essentielles à préserver. La mobilisation de ses populations autour de projets structurants pourrait contribuer à renforcer son attractivité et à ouvrir de nouvelles perspectives économiques. UNE RESPONSABILITÉ PARLEMENTAIRE AU SERVICE DES CITOYENS En prenant la parole devant ses collègues parlementaires, le député a également témoigné son respect au Président de l'Assemblée nationale et à l'ensemble de l'institution, dont le rôle demeure essentiel dans le débat public, la représentation des citoyens et l'examen des grandes questions nationales. Sa démarche rappelle qu'être député ne consiste pas uniquement à occuper un siège au sein d'une institution. C'est aussi participer aux rencontres institutionnelles, porter les préoccupations de sa circonscription, défendre les intérêts des populations et contribuer à la recherche de solutions durables. En saluant la décision du Président de la République concernant Wanindara, l'Honorable Mamadou Bhoye Bah inscrit son intervention dans une perspective de dialogue institutionnel et de développement au bénéfice des citoyens. L'enjeu est désormais de poursuivre les efforts afin que Sonfonia puisse bénéficier d'infrastructures à la hauteur de son évolution, que ses femmes disposent de meilleures opportunités, que sa jeunesse trouve davantage de perspectives et que les familles vivent dans un environnement sécurisé et favorable à leur épanouissement. Car le développement d'une commune ne se mesure pas seulement à son expansion démographique, mais aussi à la qualité de ses infrastructures, aux opportunités offertes à sa jeunesse, à la place accordée à ses femmes et à la dignité de ses populations. Sonfonia mérite une attention soutenue, des investissements structurants et une vision de développement à la mesure de son importance dans le paysage urbain guinéen. Honorable Mamadou Bhoye Bah Député de la commune de Sonfonia. items.title: SAFF Championship: Pakistan cruise past Maldives 3-0, close in on semi-final spot
items.description: Pakistan revived their semi-final hopes in the SAFF Championship with a commanding 3-0 victory over Maldives in their second Group B fixture at the National Football Stadium in Dhaka on Sunday. A first-half brace from Najeebullah Bettani, alongside an early penalty converted by McKeal Aroon Abdullah, helped Pakistan register their first victory of the tournament and put themselves in a strong position to qualify for the last four. Pakistan made an aggressive start and took the lead in the fourth minute when they were awarded a penalty. McKeal Abdullah stepped up and calmly converted from the spot to give the Green Shirts an early advantage. Pakistan continued to press forward and doubled their lead through Najeebullah, who produced a well-timed finish after Junaid Shah delivered an excellent cross from the left. Najeebullah made a perfectly timed run into the box, got ahead of his marker and poked the ball home. The forward then completed his brace with a superb individual effort. With Pakistan defending deep in their own half, the ball was cleared upfield, where Najeebullah brought it under control on the right before unleashing a powerful strike past the helpless Maldives goalkeeper. Pakistan’s three-goal advantage at half-time reflected their attacking efficiency, with the side making the most of their opportunities to put the contest beyond their opponents. Despite enjoying slightly more possession, Maldives struggled to translate it into meaningful attacking opportunities. Pakistan, meanwhile, were more threatening in front of goal, registering 15 shots, including five on target, compared to Maldives’ seven attempts, only one of which tested the goalkeeper. Both sides pushed for more goals after the interval, but neither could find the breakthrough as the second half ended goalless, leaving Pakistan with a convincing 3-0 victory. The result marked a significant response from Pakistan following their 3-2 defeat against arch-rivals India in their opening Group B encounter on November 5. Pakistan had trailed 3-0 at half-time in that match before producing a spirited late comeback. Najeebullah and Alamgir Ghazi scored in stoppage time to reduce the deficit, but India held on to secure all three points. The 2026 SAFF Championship, running from Nov 5 to 17 in Bangladesh , features six participating teams divided into two groups. Group ‘B’ comprises Pakistan, India and Maldives, while hosts Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Bhutan are in Group ‘A’. The top two teams from each group will advance to the semi-finals. With their victory over Maldives, Pakistan have moved into a stronger position in the qualification race but must now wait for the outcome of the remaining Group ‘B’ fixture between India and Maldives, scheduled for Nov 11. Maldives will need a substantial victory over India to overtake Pakistan in the group standings and secure qualification. Otherwise, Pakistan and India will progress to the semi-finals. For Pakistan, the emphatic win provides a timely boost after their opening defeat and puts them within touching distance of a place in the last four.

items.title: Novembre bleu: le personnel de l’hôpital Amadou Sakhir Mbaye de Louga sensibilise aux cancers masculins
items.description: Afin de sensibiliser les populations aux cancers masculins, notamment ceux de la prostate et des testicules, le personnel du Centre hospitalier régional Amadou Sakhir Mbaye et la Team randonnée pédestre de Louga ont sillonné, ce dimanche, les artères de la capitale du Ndiambour. Cette initiative s’inscrit dans le cadre de la campagne « Novembre Bleu ». Cette randonnée pédestre a enregistré une forte mobilisation des autorités administratives locales, des chefs de service ainsi que des représentants des collectivités territoriales. « À l’image des grands hôpitaux du pays disposant de services d’urologie, des activités de sensibilisation aux cancers de la prostate et des testicules sont organisées durant tout le mois de novembre », a déclaré le Dr Ibrahima Diabaté, chirurgien urologue au Centre hospitalier régional Amadou Sakhir Mbaye de Louga. Selon lui, « Novembre Bleu » est avant tout une campagne dédiée à la sensibilisation et au dépistage des cancers masculins. Le spécialiste a révélé que son service enregistre entre deux et trois nouveaux cas de cancer de la prostate par mois. « Les cancers de la prostate que nous recevons sont généralement diagnostiqués à un stade très avancé. Dans ces conditions, les possibilités de guérison définitive sont pratiquement inexistantes », a-t-il déploré. Il a précisé que, dans la plupart de ces situations, le traitement palliatif reste la seule alternative. Toutefois, le Dr Ibrahima Diabaté a souligné que le cancer de la prostate peut être guéri lorsqu’il est diagnostiqué et pris en charge suffisamment tôt. À cet effet, il a exhorté les hommes âgés de 45 ans et plus à consulter un urologue pour se faire dépister. Dans cette même dynamique, le Dr Diabaté a annoncé l’organisation de consultations médicales gratuites durant tout le mois de novembre. « Tout homme souhaitant bénéficier d’une consultation est invité à se rapprocher du service social de l’hôpital pour y laisser ses coordonnées », a-t-il indiqué. Falel PAM

items.title: Troops neutralise suspected criminal, arrest five in Plateau
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – Troops of Operation Enduring Peace (OPEP) have neutralised a suspected notorious criminal in Wase Local Government Area and arrested five suspected phone snatchers during a raid on a hotel in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. The operations also led to the recovery of 26 mobile phones and other items suspected to be stolen, including laptops, earpods and power banks. Military sources disclosed that the suspected criminal, identified as Abubakar Ango, was arrested on November 4 by troops of Sector 2 OPEP at Kukawa village in Wase. “At about 7:20 a.m. on November 6, during interrogation, the suspect reportedly confessed to involvement in several criminal activities and agreed to lead troops to his gang’s hideouts in a village forest,” the sources said. They explained that the mission was intended to facilitate the recovery of weapons and possible arrest of other members of the gang. “However, while being escorted to the location, the suspect allegedly attempted to seize the rifle of one of the soldiers, prompting an immediate response that resulted in his neutralisation,” they said. On the Jos operation, the sources said troops of Sector 1 OPEP arrested five suspected criminals during a raid on a Hotel along Baring Road in Jos North. “The troops, while on patrol, responded to a report of phone snatching at about 9 p.m. on November 6, 2026. The stolen phone was reportedly tracked to the Hotel within the area, prompting troops to conduct a raid on the facility,” the sources said. They disclosed that the five suspects were found in possession of the tracked phone, while a further search led to the recovery of 26 mobile phones, 27 pouches, three MP devices, two earpods, an HP laptop, a knife and four power banks. “The vehicle belonging to the suspects was also towed to the headquarters of Sector 1 for a comprehensive search,” the sources added. “The suspects and recovered exhibits have been taken into custody for further investigation and necessary action,” the sources said. Confirming the two incidents, the spokesperson for Operation Enduring Peace, Captain Polycarp Chinonso Oteh, urged residents to cooperate with the military and other security agencies by providing credible and timely information to assist ongoing operations. “We urge members of the public to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements and activities to security operatives,” Oteh said. He stressed that the cooperation of residents was critical to the success of ongoing efforts to combat criminal activities and restore lasting peace across Plateau State. “We assure residents of the military’s continued commitment to protecting lives and property and urge them not to hesitate to share useful information with security agencies,” he said.
