items.title: Iran-US tensions rise amid maritime incidents and diplomatic efforts
items.description: Following the US midterm election, tensions in the Middle East are mounting as Iran and the United States step up military preparations amid growing concerns over a possible new outbreak of open conflict. Explosions heard in Iran Several explosions were heard on Saturday night in the southern Iranian counties of Qeshm, Sirik, Jask and Bandar Abbas, state-run IRIB TV reported. It said it was not yet clear whether the blasts resulted from an enemy attack or from the Iranian armed forces firing at "violating" vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. The official news agency IRNA earlier reported two explosions on Qeshm Island, citing its correspondent as saying that the blasts occurred on the island. However, the semi-official Tasnim news agency quoted an informed source as saying that the sounds were linked to the Iranian armed forces' management of maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz and that no projectile had struck the island. Vessels hit in Strait of Hormuz Passage through the Strait of Hormuz remains hazardous as both Iran and the US are targeting tankers passing through the crucial waterway. The navy of Iran's Islamic Revolution Guard Corps (IRGC) said early Sunday two "violating" oil tankers attempting to pass through an "unauthorized" route in the Strait of Hormuz caught fire after hitting naval mines. In a statement on the IRGC's official news outlet, Sepah News, the navy said that one tanker hit mines east of the strait and the other while crossing the waterway. Both vessels had turned off navigation and GPS systems and were burning following the explosions, it added. The IRGC warned that any vessel cooperating with the "aggressive" US Army and entering the "unauthorized" region in the strait in defiance of Iranian regulations would "definitely" hit naval mines. Meanwhile, US Central Command (CENTCOM) said on social media platform X that its forces had disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman after its civilian crew "ignored repeated warnings and attempted to violate the naval blockade against Iran multiple times." "A US military aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of St. Kitts-flagged M/V Huda, disabling the ship after CENTCOM forces directed the crew to abandon targeted spaces. The cargo vessel tried to depart regional waters after visiting an Iranian port," it added. Diplomatic efforts underway Meanwhile, both the US and Iran are still conducting diplomatic efforts aimed at negotiations. According to Axios, US Vice President JD Vance has personally participated in indirect talks with Iran over the past two weeks aimed at reaching a new ceasefire and resuming nuclear negotiations. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi also made a flurry of phone calls in the past two days with counterparts from 12 countries. Sharing details about his calls on X, Araghchi listed the nations as Oman, Egypt, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Cyprus, Türkiye, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Tunisia, Iraq and Pakistan. He said they discussed regional and international developments and that he reiterated Tehran’s core positions. He stressed that the national sovereignty of all states must be respected, aggression and threats must end, and destructive foreign interference must be avoided. He also noted that countries in the region bear responsibility to prevent further security escalations. (With input from agencies)

items.title: Asempa FM’s Ekosiisen wins Best Radio Programme of the Year (Ghanaian Language)
items.description: Asempa FM’s flagship current affairs programme, Ekosiisen , has won the Best Radio Programme of the Year (Ghanaian Language) award at the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards. The award recognises the programme’s work in Twi-language broadcasting and its contribution to public discourse on national issues. The recognition came on the same night the programme’s host, Philip Osei Bonsu, popularly known as O.B., was named the 2026 GJA Journalist of the Year. The two awards marked a notable night for Asempa FM, a subsidiary of the Multimedia Group Limited, with both the programme and its host receiving top honours. In an earlier interview, O.B. attributed the programme’s recognition to the commitment and professionalism of his team. “This recognition truly reflects the hard work and sense of professionalism of my incredible team on EKOSIISEN. It also reflects the sense of duty and dedication to my chosen professions: Broadcast Journalism and Law,” he stated. Ekosiisen is Asempa FM’s current affairs programme, hosted by O.B. It covers political developments, public affairs and national issues in the Twi language. The 30th GJA Media Awards were held in Accra on Saturday, November 7, 2026, under the theme, “Celebrating Excellence, Advancing Media Freedom and Combating Hate Speech in the Digital Age”.

items.title: SMOKERS’ CORNER: Bollywood’s Hold on Pakistan
items.description: It never ceases to baffle me how Bollywood films, frequently stuffed with overt, heavy-handed propaganda against Pakistan, effortlessly climb to the top of Netflix’s trending charts in Pakistan. This dichotomy is by no means an indictment of the patriotism of Pakistani viewers. It is, instead, a fascinating sociological puzzle worth exploring. The contradiction feels all the more glaring given that the Indian state openly pursues policies aimed at destabilising Pakistan, notably through its now hardly discreet patronage of proxy networks such as the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and armed Baloch separatist factions. Let’s investigate. One can posit that, ever since the 1980s, when Pakistan’s cultural trajectory was gradually shifted to the right by a military dictatorship in league with moralist groups, local audiences began starving for high-production cinematic entertainment. They craved slick action choreography, sweeping soundtracks and genuine star power and/or elements that Pakistani media industries, crippled by social constraints and lack of adequate financial resources, struggled to supply. As a result, every time a high-budget Bollywood spectacle drops on a popular streaming platform and, crucially, in a language (Hindi) that is effortlessly understood across Pakistan, this acts as an irresistible pull. How do Pakistani audiences reconcile their appetite for Indian cinema with the hostile political narratives increasingly embedded in Bollywood films? So how do Pakistani viewers cope with the dichotomy of putting anti-Pakistan Indian films at the top on streaming services? My own ongoing research suggests that they handle this by neatly compartmentalising and isolating certain geopolitical contexts. They treat the screen as an insulated fantasy world, where entertainment value trumps geopolitical friction. This allows them to relish the cinematic spectacle while disconnecting themselves from the underlying anti-Pakistan hostility of the movies’ narratives. Illustration by Abro This is bolstered by a deeply ingrained historical and linguistic familiarity. Shared idioms, musical heritage and emotional resonance allow cross-border cultural products to easily bypass the psychological and cultural barriers that typically confront other foreign media products. In my discussions on this phenomenon with various observers, including figures within Pakistan’s cultural industries, a clear pattern emerges. Pakistanis consume hostile (but glossy) Indian content not as an endorsement of the content’s ideological messaging, but through a lens of detachment and often outright amusement. This detachment creates a shield, enabling Pakistani viewers to enjoy a Bollywood blockbuster without feeling that their national identity is compromised by a piece of theatrical fiction. So far, so good. But there is another side to this phenomenon. This one is tied to the mechanics of what is often referred to as “soft-power hegemony.” As the early 20th-century Italian theorist Antonio Gramsci posited, a dominant force maintains control not only through physical state power but by manufacturing cultural consent. This shapes the everyday values, aesthetic desires and the social logic of subordinate groups. The rightward shift in Pakistan’s social realm from the 1980s onwards was driven as much by state-sanctioned ‘Islamism’ as it was by the gradual ‘Indianisation’ of the Pakistani middle-class lifestyle. It is this class that often dominates the social/cultural, economic and political terrains of most countries. Now let’s explore how cross-border soft-power hegemony operates in this context. As state-enforced puritanism under a right-wing dictatorship in Pakistan in the 1980s restricted urban leisure, it inadvertently created a wide cultural vacuum. Indian popular culture, initially smuggled via VCR tapes in the 1980s and later broadcast through satellite television and digital platforms, swiftly stepped into this void. For over four decades now, Bollywood blockbusters, Indian soap operas, and wedding aesthetics subtly rewired the Pakistani middle-class imagination, embedding Indian linguistic tropes, fashion paradigms and ritualistic sensibilities into the domestic fabric. This occurred at the expense of Pakistan’s own popular culture, which was dismantled and replaced with an enforced, cosmetic veneer of state-sanctioned piety. This synthetic moral order was cynically crafted and therefore unable to resist the pull of Indian cultural products, even as these products grew increasingly hostile towards Pakistan’s existential narratives. Indian cultural products engage Pakistani audiences by treating them as cultural subordinates, moulding their mindset to mirror and reinforce India’s broader political and cultural hegemony in the region. These products have become cultural weapons, as effective as the Hollywood products that leaked into former communist countries during the Cold War. Sometimes overtly and sometimes subtly, Hollywood productions during that period equated glossy Western consumerism with democracy and freedom. Communist audiences were bagged. Securing a pair of Levi’s jeans became an act of fighting communist tyranny. Nevertheless, watching Bollywood films wouldn’t be as harmful, though, if India and Pakistan regularly exchanged movies and media. When two countries trade media back and forth, money keeps extreme nationalism in check. Filmmakers treat their work like global brands, avoiding storyline choices that would offend audiences in neighbouring markets and hurt sales. However, when governments ban this trade, commercial restraint disappears. Without foreign box-office revenue on the line, entertainment media easily transforms into political propaganda. The Pakistani government bans Indian movies from local cinemas. This means that Bollywood faces zero financial risk when portraying Pakistan in a negative light. Free from foreign box-office stakes, its primary goal is to cater to hyper-nationalist audiences at home and exhibit how superior this strand of nationalism is compared to Pakistani nationalism. Indeed, the Indian state too maintains a blanket ban on Pakistani cultural products. But the fact is, Bollywood continues to profit off Pakistani viewers through foreign streaming platforms that collect monthly subscription fees. That money ends up in the pockets of Indian filmmakers. The ‘detached consumption’ habit of Pakistani audiences casually watching even the most absurd anti-Pakistan propaganda films made by India can further mutate into something odder. For instance, I was witness to some corporate brands in Pakistan asking their advertising agencies to hire ‘Indian talent’ for their commercial campaigns. While cross-border collaboration is not inherently unusual, the timing was astounding. This occurred during the 2025 military confrontation between India and Pakistan, right when Indian drones were targeting buildings in Pakistani cities. The sheer tone-deafness of it was baffling, as if these corporate executives lived in a bubble, where nothing existed outside their fixation on all things Indian. Bollywood is a powerhouse, while Pakistan’s cinema industry has struggled with economic instability and lack of support. As a result, one country easily exports its political views while the other lacks the industry size to offer a strong counter-narrative. It just can’t or is unwilling to go beyond making terrible rom-coms. Cultural consumption stops being a shared exchange and becomes a one-sided relationship, where the larger industry routinely demonises and mocks its cross-border audience without any pushback. While Pakistanis may grin and say they are watching Indian cinematic propaganda to make fun of it, the truth is, the joke is really on them. They are paying Pakistani money to mock it. If so many Pakistanis can successfully boycott giant commercial brands and replace them with local ones as a protest against Israel’s genocide in Gaza, what’s stopping them from ignoring Bollywood films that exude obvious anti-Pakistan propaganda? Published in Dawn, EOS, November 8th, 2026

items.title: Woman alleges harassment by ex-husband on court premises
items.description: LAHORE: A British Pakistani woman pursuing maintenance litigation against her former husband for their three daughters has alleged harassment and intimidation by him on the court’s premises. In her application submitted to the Islampura police, the complainant, Laleen, alleged that she had visited the sessions court for a hearing against her ex-husband, a businessman. She had obtained a Khula (judicial divorce) from him seven years earlier and a guardian court had decided the matter of the daughters’ custody in her favour, which attained finality. The woman alleged that upon exiting the courtroom, she was confronted by her former husband alongside unidentified individuals. She claimed the men harassed her, hurled verbal abuse and continued issuing threats even in the judge’s chamber. LHC dismisses plea challenging guardian court’s decision on maintenance allowance for three daughters According to the complaint filed on Oct 23, the former husband repeatedly demanded custody of their daughters, issued death threats, and physically shoved her. The complainant further alleged that the suspects prevented her from dialling the police helpline (15) or immediately reaching the police station, subjecting her to severe mental distress before she managed to escape. Despite providing video evidence, she alleged, the police were reluctant to register a case. However, the inquiry officer concerned at Islampura Police Station told Dawn that the matter had been investigated but no cognisable offence was made out. Laleen has appealed to Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, urging her to intervene and ensure justice. “I have been cleared in numerous malicious cases,” she said. “Given CM Maryam Nawaz’s work for women and children, I request her support in the matter,” the woman stated. She also seeks removal of her youngest daughter’s name from the Exit Control List. A family court had awarded each daughter Rs100,000 per month in maintenance from January 2017, along with educational expenses and a 10pc annual increase. The father had challenged the decree, arguing that the maintenance amount was excessive and beyond his means. However, the Lahore High Court (LHC) upheld the decision, dismissing his appeal and ruling that a father cannot evade his financial obligations by concealing his assets and income. The court noted that the educational expenses reflected the standard of living the children had enjoyed before the marital dispute and that a father could not reduce that standard merely because the children were now residing with their mother. It held that the maintenance must correspond to the children’s needs, social background, educational requirements and the father’s financial standing. However, the children have yet to receive maintenance, since the execution proceedings are still pending. In a recent judgement, the LHC underscored the systemic issue of delays in execution of decrees, observing that prolonged enforcement proceedings defeat the very purpose of adjudication and reduce court judgements to “mere paper declarations.” The court noted that although cases are decided within the statutory timelines, the real hardship for litigants often begins at the execution stage. Published in Dawn, November 8th, 2026

items.title: Sindh CM declares Tharparkar drought-hit, orders relief measures
items.description: KARACHI: Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah on Saturday declared Tharparkar a drought-affected district after reviewing the situation and the severe crop losses. He directed the relevant departments to begin relief work immediately and to ensure that drinking water and essential supplies were available to the affected population. Presiding over a meeting at the CM House, Mr Shah was briefed on drought-like conditions in all seven talukas of the district. The meeting was attended, among others, by MNA Dr Mahesh Malani; MPAs Dost Muhammad Rahimoon, Qasim Soomro, Faqeer Sher Muhammad Bilalani and Arbab Lutfullah; Chief Secretary Asif Hyder Shah; Senior Member of the Board of Revenue Khalid Hyder Shah; and Mirpurkhas Commissio­ner Shahmir Bhutto. According to a press statement issued by the CM House, the briefing revealed that all seven talukas were facing drought-like conditions, with 85 to 90 per cent of cultivated crops either destroyed or rendered unproductive. The agriculture extension department put crop losses at around 90 per cent, while field reports from assistant commissioners and mukhtiarkars confirmed that only 10 to 15 per cent of crops had survived. The chief minister expressed serious concern over the effect of inadequate and poorly distributed rainfall on agriculture, livestock and livelihoods in the district. He said the situation demanded immediate government intervention, particularly to protect livestock, a major source of income for the people of the desert district. He directed the chief secretary to ensure that all non-functional reverse osmosis (RO) plants were repaired and restored on a priority basis. The authorities were also told to identify faults in existing water supply sources and make them fully functional so that local communities had uninterrupted access to drinking water. Mr Shah further asked the chief secretary to assess the feasibility of laying a dedicated water supply line from Naukot to Mithi to provide the people of Mithi with a sustainable and reliable supply. All technical and administrative requirements should be examined urgently, he said, so that a long-term solution to the area’s water shortage could be developed. The chief minister also stressed the need for urgent arrangements to address the shortage of fodder and protect livestock from the effects of drought. He directed the departments concerned to coordinate their efforts and ensure that relief reached the affected areas without delay. The briefing noted that rainfall during this year’s monsoon had been uneven. Although seasonal totals ranged from 181mm to 273mm across the seven talukas, September rainfall was particularly low, at between 1mm and 36mm. As a result, crops and natural grass dried out before they could mature. The CM said the provincial government would stand by the people of Tharparkar during this difficult period. He directed the administration to remain vigilant, monitor the situation closely and ensure that no affected community was left without essential support. Published in Dawn, November 8th, 2026

items.title: Tents flooded as heavy rain hits Gaza
items.description: GAZA CITY: Heavy rain on Saturday flooded tens of thousands of displaced people’s tents in the war-devastated Gaza, Palestinian authorities said, leaving many of them without shelter. About “70,000 tents sheltering tens of thousands of displaced people were flooded on the first day” of rains, the Hamas-run government media office stated. There were also reports of “collapse of dozens of cracked walls and roofs, which caused injuries”, some critical, in various areas of the tiny territory, it added. Civil defence spokesman Mahmoud Bassal told AFP his teams had received more than 1,500 calls during the night from residents requesting urgent assistance after their tents were flooded, explaining that the agency “is operating without any equipment or capabilities”. Civil society groups warn of disease outbreaks, urge pressure on Israel to allow entry of aid “We have issued an urgent distress call to the international community and hum­a­nitarian organisations to intervene immediately to save hundreds of thousands of displaced people from the flooding of their tents. We cannot face the consequences of this storm on our own,” he said. A coalition of Palestinian civil society organisations has warned of “the catastrophe that has come to threaten the lives of hundreds of thousands of residents”, pointing to the risk of the spread of diseases and epidemics. The coalition, which includes dozens of local institutions and organisations, called for “pressure on Israel to allow the entry of humanitarian aid without restrictions”. A fragile ceasefire came into effect on Oct 10, 2025, after two years of war. However, despite the ceasefire agreement reached with Egyptian, Qatari, and American mediation, the Israeli army continued air strikes and ground operations on an almost daily basis. Mustafa Qazzaat, a member of the Gaza city council and an official in the Strip’s emergency committee, said Israel did not allow prefabricated homes to shelter the displaced in Gaza even after the announcement of the so-called truce, and only permitted the entry of limited numbers of tents. He said Gaza “needs 200,000 prefabricated homes urgently, in addition to the entry of heavy machinery to remove the rubble of destroyed homes and buildings, open main roads, and urgently provide electricity and heating”. Published in Dawn, November 8th, 2026

items.title: Asempa FM’s Philip Osei Bonsu ‘O.B.’ named 2026 GJA Journalist of the Year
items.description: Asempa FM’s Philip Osei Bonsu, popularly known as O.B., has been named the 2026 Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Journalist of the Year at the 30th GJA Media Awards in Accra. The award, the highest individual honour at the Association’s annual awards ceremony, recognises his contribution to journalism in Ghana during the qualifying period. O.B. hosts Ekosiisen , Asempa FM’s late-afternoon current affairs programme, known for its coverage of political and public affairs. He also serves as Programmes Manager at Asempa FM, a subsidiary of the Multimedia Group Limited. Beyond broadcasting, he is a qualified lawyer who was called to the Ghana Bar in October 2024 after completing his legal training at the Ghana School of Law. He holds a First Class Honours degree in Linguistics and Theatre Arts from the University of Ghana, an MSc in Corporate Communication and Public Affairs with Distinction from Robert Gordon University in Scotland, and an LLB from Central University. He was also a Tullow Scholar and a 2017 Mandela Washington Fellow at the University of San Diego. In January 2026, O.B. was named among the personalities featured in Avance Media’s inaugural Top 100 Ghanaians Powerlist 2025. He was recognised in the media category for his work as host of Ekosiisen . Reacting to the recognition at the time, he credited his production team for its contribution to the programme’s work. “This recognition truly reflects the hard work and sense of professionalism of my incredible team on EKOSIISEN. It also reflects the sense of duty and dedication to my chosen professions: Broadcast Journalism and Law,” he stated. The 30th GJA Media Awards were held on Saturday, November 7, 2026, under the theme, “Celebrating Excellence, Advancing Media Freedom and Combating Hate Speech in the Digital Age”. The ceremony brought together journalists, media organisations and other stakeholders to recognise achievements in the media industry. Luv FM’s Clinton Yeboah was also among the award recipients, winning the Best Radio Feature category.

items.title: Mort du chef de canton de Solenzo : 19 accusés bientôt devant le juge
items.description: Deux ans après les événements du 24 novembre 2024 ayant coûté la vie au chef de canton de Solenzo, 19 personnes seront jugées du 9 au 11 novembre 2026 devant la chambre criminelle du Tribunal de grande instance de Dédougou. L’affaire de la mort du chef de canton de Solenzo connaît une nouvelle étape judiciaire. Dix-neuf (19) accusés comparaîtront devant la chambre criminelle du Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Dédougou, délocalisée à Solenzo, les 9, 10 et 11 novembre 2026. L’annonce a été faite par le Procureur du Faso près le TGI de Dédougou dans un communiqué. Les audiences se tiendront dans la salle des fêtes de la mairie de Solenzo, dans la province des Banwa. Un seul dossier figure au rôle de cette session criminelle. Il porte sur les événements du 24 novembre 2024, marqués par une manifestation au cours de laquelle le chef de canton de Solenzo a perdu la vie. Au total, 19 accusés devront répondre des faits qui leur sont reprochés devant la juridiction. Un premier procès correctionnel en décembre 2024 Cette affaire a déjà connu un premier épisode judiciaire. Le volet correctionnel avait été examiné le 20 décembre 2024 à Bobo-Dioulasso. À l’issue de cette audience, 15 prévenus sur les 26 ayant comparu avaient été condamnés à différentes peines. La prochaine audience permettra ainsi à la justice d’examiner le volet criminel de cette affaire, dans le cadre du traitement judiciaire des événements ayant conduit au décès du chef de canton. Une audience foraine pour rapprocher la justice des populations La tenue de cette session à Solenzo s’inscrit dans une démarche de proximité judiciaire. En délocalisant les audiences dans cette localité, le TGI de Dédougou entend faciliter l’accès des populations à la justice. Le Procureur du Faso a, à cet effet, réaffirmé sa disponibilité à œuvrer pour une justice plus proche des citoyens, diligente et à leur écoute. L’article Mort du chef de canton de Solenzo : 19 accusés bientôt devant le juge est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Herzog taps Eisenkot to form next Israeli government
items.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog announced Saturday evening that he would task Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming the next government following consultations with political parties. Herzog has invited Eisenkot to the President's Residence on Sunday at 5 p.m. to formally receive the mandate, according to a statement from the Office of the President. "This is the time to establish a national emergency government. I will do anything possible to prove us worthy," Eisenkot said on the social media platform X following the announcement. Under Israeli law, the former military chief has 28 days to assemble a governing coalition and can request a 14-day extension from the president. If he fails, Herzog may assign the task to another candidate, or at least 61 members of the 120-seat parliament can ask the president to entrust the mandate to a candidate of their choice. If these efforts also fail, the parliament will be dissolved and the country will hold new elections. In the parliamentary recommendations submitted to Herzog, Eisenkot received backing from 48 lawmakers from four opposition-bloc parties, in addition to 19 representatives of Arab-led parties. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was recommended by 46 lawmakers, while the seven members of the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism party declined to endorse either candidate. Despite receiving the most recommendations, analysts say Eisenkot faces a challenging path to securing a 61-seat majority, with divisions within the opposition over cooperation with Arab parties and disagreements with the two ultra-Orthodox parties, which together hold 13 seats. Earlier Saturday, Netanyahu called for a national unity government, warning against a government that relies on support from Arab parties and accusing them of seeking Israel's destruction. Netanyahu added that a national unity government should include all parties in the current governing coalition, alongside "all the Zionist parties that want to protect our country."

items.title: BoG Governor Johnson Asiama says professional journalism is vital in fighting digital misinformation
items.description: Bank of Ghana Governor, Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, has described professional journalism as “society’s compass”, saying it remains essential in helping citizens navigate the growing challenges of the digital age. Speaking at the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards in Accra on Saturday, November 7, 2026, he said technological advancements had transformed how information is created, distributed and consumed, presenting both opportunities and challenges for society. Dr Asiama noted that while digital platforms had expanded opportunities for citizens to participate in public discussions and share information, they had also contributed to the spread of misinformation, disinformation, online abuse, misleading data and hate speech. “Although digital platforms have created unprecedented opportunities for citizens to get involved and share information, they have also brought significant challenges, including misinformation, disinformation, online abuse, misleading data and hate speech,” he said. The Governor said professional journalism plays a critical role in helping citizens distinguish facts from falsehood, evidence from speculation and informed analysis from sensationalism. He described journalists as guardians of public discourse whose work contributes to social cohesion, informed debate and the protection of democratic principles. “As guardians of public discourse, journalists are essential for building social unity, encouraging well-informed discussions, and safeguarding democratic principles,” he stated. Dr Asiama also highlighted the media’s role in making complex economic and financial issues accessible to the public. He cited monetary policy decisions, inflation trends, financial sector reforms, exchange rate movements and digital financial innovations as issues that require accurate and balanced reporting to help citizens understand developments affecting their lives. He said effective journalism translates such technical subjects into information that the public can understand and use. The 30th GJA Media Awards were held under the theme, “Celebrating Excellence, Advancing Media Freedom and Combating Hate Speech in the Digital Age”. The theme highlights the need to protect press freedom while promoting responsible journalism in an increasingly digital information environment. The Bank of Ghana has also pledged to continue supporting initiatives that recognise excellence in economic and financial reporting.

items.title: Trump offers UFC CEO Dana White White House press secretary job
items.description: US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that he had offered Dana White, president and CEO of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC), the position of White House press secretary. In a post on Truth Social, Trump said he had asked White to bring assistants with him and named several UFC fighters. "I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States," Trump wrote. "I have requested that he bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country." "We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!" Trump added. Shortly after Trump's announcement, White posted an image on Instagram showing himself standing behind the White House press briefing podium, accompanied by the caption "On to the next chapter," potentially signaling his willingness to accept the offer.

items.title: Egypt sacks coach Hossam Hassan over ‘negative impact’ on team image
items.description: Egypt coach Hossam Hassan was sacked on Saturday for what the soccer federation cited as “a negative impact on the positive image of the team.” The Egyptian Football Association did not elaborate in a statement, adding only that “maintaining the team’s stability is a paramount priority” that cannot be compromised. Egyptian media believed the decision had more to do with Hassan’s personal life than rumors of disagreements with Egyptian players, including star forward Mohamed Salah. Egypt’s Supreme Council for Media Regulation banned Hassan last week from appearing in all media outlets, an unprecedented decision against a national coach. That followed disputes in Hassan’s personal life becoming public. Hassan was appointed Egypt coach in 2024 and became the first former Egypt player to coach the national team at a World Cup this year. Egypt was knocked out by Argentina in the last 16. The EFA immediately replaced Hassan with Ali Maher, a long-time head coach in the Egyptian Premier League currently leading fourth-placed Ceramica Cleopatra. Maher must get quickly up to speed. Egypt plays Malawi on Nov. 13 and 17 in qualifying for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations. Egypt leads Group B.

items.title: BoG introduces economic and financial journalism award with international training opportunities at 30th GJA Media Awards
items.description: The Bank of Ghana (BoG) has announced a new award scheme to recognise excellence in economic and financial journalism, offering winners opportunities for international exposure, professional training and further studies. The Governor’s Economic and Financial Story of the Year Award was announced by Bank of Ghana Governor, Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, in a speech he personally delivered at the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards at the Palms Convention Centre, La Palm Royal Beach Hotel, Accra, on Saturday, November 7, 2026. The package includes sponsorship for the winner to attend either the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Spring Meetings or Annual Meetings, a laptop computer and a one-year internet data subscription. It will also provide access to professional fellowships with institutions such as the Thomson Foundation, the Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism and accredited local journalism training centres. Other opportunities include scholarships for further studies in media, communications and related fields, as well as professional exchange programmes with international media organisations such as Bloomberg and Reuters. “Our objective is simple: to invest in the development of journalists who can continue to elevate the quality of economic and financial reporting in Ghana,” the Governor said. The Governor described the media as an essential partner in helping the public understand economic and financial developments. He noted that issues such as monetary policy, inflation, financial sector reforms, exchange rate movements and digital financial innovations could be complex, making accurate and accessible reporting important to public understanding. “It is through accurate, balanced, and insightful reporting that these issues are translated into information citizens can understand and use,” he said. The Governor also emphasised the importance of effective communication in central banking, saying public understanding of the Bank’s policies was critical to their effectiveness. “Our policies are most effective when they are clearly understood by the public. Transparency, credibility, and accountability require open and effective engagement with all stakeholders, including the media,” he said. The award forms part of the Bank’s efforts to encourage specialised reporting on economic and financial issues and promote greater public understanding of developments in the sector. It is expected to provide journalists with opportunities to build their reporting skills and deepen their knowledge of issues that affect businesses, households and the wider economy.

items.title: AmCham Shanghai president: CIIE connects US firms to China's market
items.description: The American Food and Agriculture Pavilion officially opened at the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) in Shanghai on November 6. Organized by AmCham Shanghai and the US Department of Agriculture, this marks the pavilion's fourth year at the expo. And it's off to a roaring start, with a record 40-plus trade associations and companies participating, and more than $650 million in deals signed on day one for products like sorghum, wheat, beef and animal nutrition. Ahead of the expo, CGTN Digital journalist Shen Shiwei spoke with Eric Zheng, president of AmCham Shanghai, about how the event connects US companies, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, with the Chinese market. Zheng, who has attended every CIIE since its inception, says the event demonstrates China's openness to foreign products and services, and highlights the highly complementary trade relationship between the world’s two largest economies.

items.title: Real Madrid beat Valencia to move level on points with leaders Barcelona
items.description: Real Madrid moved level on points with La Liga leaders Barcelona after a comfortable victory at struggling Valencia. Captain Federico Valverde opened the scoring in the 28th minute with a crisp, low drive from 20 yards after Kylian Mbappe’s free-kick came back off the wall. Eight minutes later, Jose Mourinho’s side doubled their advantage as Arda Guler volleyed in from six yards after Jude Bellingham’s cutback was deflected kindly into his path. The visitors remained in control in the second half and the result was put beyond doubt 15 minutes from time when Guler found Mbappe, who rounded the goalkeeper to score his 13th league goal of the campaign. It only got worse for Valencia as captain Jose Gaya was sent off for scything down Mbappe with the striker set to streak clear on goal. A fourth straight league win means only goal difference keeps Real off top spot, although Barca can restore their three-point advantage when they play third-placed Atletico Madrid on Sunday (20:00 GMT). Valencia stay 19th, a point from safety, after a seventh league defeat from 12 games. The game was paused nine minutes into the first half to allow players and fans to pay tribute to Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, who died after suffering a serious injury during a Spanish second-division match, with a minute’s applause.

items.title: Government renews commitment to unravel Ahmed Suale’s murder – Kwakye Ofosu
items.description: The government has reaffirmed its commitment to unraveling the murder of investigative journalist Ahmed Suale, whose killing in January 2019 remains unsolved. Speaking on behalf of President John Dramani Mahama at the 30th GJA Media Awards in Accra, Minister of State in charge of Government Communications, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, said journalists in Ghana had lost their lives in the pursuit of accountability. He cited the killing of Mr Suale, an investigative journalist with Tiger Eye PI, and said the government remained committed to finding those responsible. “Journalists in our country lost their lives in pursuit of accountability, and I refer to the unfortunate killing of Ahmed Suale, whose murder remains unsolved, and the government remains committed to unraveling it,” he stated. Mr Kwakye Ofosu also acknowledged the dangers faced by journalists who publish reports considered uncomfortable by powerful interests. He referred to journalists in the northern part of the country who, he said, had to flee for their lives after publishing such reports. “Our words in support of free speech must not ring hollow, especially when in the north, through the past, journalists had to flee our country for fear of their lives because they published uncomfortable truths,” he stated. Ahmed Suale was shot dead in Madina, Accra, in January 2019. He was part of the Tiger Eye PI investigative team and had worked on investigations into corruption and other matters of public interest. His killing remains unresolved, with the GJA and other media stakeholders continuing to call for justice. The government’s latest pledge comes amid broader concerns about journalist safety and the need to protect media practitioners from intimidation and attacks. Mr Kwakye Ofosu said the government remained committed to pursuing the circumstances surrounding Suale’s murder and protecting journalists across the country.

items.title: Ghana Tennis Federation boss, Aboagye Duah, elected as West Africa Prez & Veep at Tennis Africa
items.description: LUANDA, ANGOLA, 7 November 2026 — Ghana has secured a significant leadership position in African tennis following the election of Mr Isaac Aboagye Duah, President of the Ghana Tennis Federation (GTF), as President of the West Africa Zone and Vice President of Tennis Africa. Mr Duah was elected unopposed at the Tennis Africa Annual General Meeting held in Luanda, Angola, filling the vacancy created by the passing of former Zone President, Ing. Ifedayo Akindoju Dayo, last year. In accordance with the Tennis Africa Constitution, the position was filled through an election at the next AGM. The West Africa Zone comprises 15 countries. Mr Duah’s election presents an opportunity for Ghana to contribute more directly to continental tennis governance and for the sub-region to strengthen cooperation in developing the sport. A Record of Inclusive Leadership Mr Duah has served as President of the Ghana Tennis Federation since 2017. His tenure has focused on inclusive governance, stakeholder engagement, and creating opportunities for the growth of tennis. Two significant initiatives stand out. First, he championed the recognition of players, coaches, officiating officials and clubs as delegates at the highest decision-making body of tennis governance in Ghana, ensuring that key stakeholders have a voice in shaping the sport’s future. Second, he has promoted an open-door policy that creates an enabling environment for tennis clubs and foundations to operate, partner with the Federation and organise internationally recognised World Tennis competitions. Under his leadership, Ghana has participated in West African junior competitions over the past nine years, achieved notable success in African 12-and-under competitions, and continued to represent the country in the Davis Cup and Billie Jean King Cup. Mr Duah also serves on the African Cup of Nations Sub-Committee of Tennis Africa, contributing to the development of continental tennis. A Vision for African Tennis Commenting on his election, Mr Duah said: “I am deeply honoured by the confidence placed in me and humbled by the opportunity to serve tennis across West Africa and the African continent. My leadership philosophy has always been anchored in inclusion, collaboration and the belief that tennis can only grow when players, coaches, officials, clubs and foundations are recognised, valued and given a meaningful voice. “I look forward to bringing this spirit of inclusive leadership to Tennis Africa. Working with our 15 West African member countries and stakeholders across the continent, we can strengthen our institutions, develop our players and officials, attract greater investment and create sustainable opportunities for the next generation. My vision is for an African tennis community that is united in purpose, strong in governance and increasingly competitive on the world stage.” His new responsibilities will provide an opportunity to promote stronger cooperation among national federations, expand junior development, strengthen institutional capacity and encourage investment in tennis infrastructure and competitions. Academic Background Mr Duah is an alumnus of the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), where he obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Chemistry. He also holds an Executive Master of Business Administration (EMBA), a Master of Arts in Leadership and Management, and a Chartered Institute of Marketing (CIM-UK) qualification as a Chartered Marketer. He received his secondary education at Pope John Senior High School and Minor Seminary in Koforidua. His election marks an important milestone for Ghanaian sports administration and offers an opportunity to strengthen the country’s contribution to tennis development across West Africa and the continent. The Ghana Tennis Federation congratulates its President on his election and looks forward to his continued service to the sport at both national and continental levels.

items.title: Government does not expect favourable headlines from media – Kwakye Ofosu
items.description: The government has reaffirmed its commitment to media freedom, saying it does not expect favourable headlines from journalists as a condition for engagement with the media. Speaking on behalf of President John Dramani Mahama at the 30th GJA Media Awards in Accra, Minister of State in charge of Government Communications, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, said the media must be free to question government, scrutinise public expenditure, investigate public institutions and examine decisions taken by public officials. He said the government recognises that a democratic administration must be prepared to respond to difficult questions and accept legitimate criticism. “We do not expect favourable headlines as a condition for engagement, nor do we expect journalists to surrender their editorial independence in the name of partnership. Indeed, a government that is confident in its democratic credentials must be prepared to answer difficult questions and accept legitimate criticism,” he stated. Mr Kwakye Ofosu said journalists must be allowed to criticise government when it falls short, acknowledge achievements when they are delivered and demand explanations whenever the public interest requires it. “The media must be free to criticise whenever there’s a shortfall, acknowledge achievements when we deliver, and demand explanations whenever the public interest requires it,” he said. The Minister also highlighted the need to protect journalists from attacks, threats and unlawful detention while carrying out their professional duties. He said allegations of attacks, including those involving security personnel, must be investigated and accountability pursued where wrongdoing is established. “No journalist should be assaulted, threatened, or unlawfully detained for undertaking a legitimate professional assignment. Allegations of attacks, including those involving security personnel, must be investigated, and where wrongdoing is established, accountability must follow,” he stated. The comments come amid concerns about the safety of journalists and the state of media freedom in Ghana. The Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) has recorded more than 50 incidents involving attacks, arrests and harassment of journalists between 2022 and January 2026. The government says it will continue to work with media stakeholders to ensure that constitutional guarantees of freedom of expression and media independence are reflected in the everyday experiences of journalists.

items.title: Threatening to kill the President and his children is criminality, not free speech – Kwakye Ofosu
items.description: Minister of State in charge of Government Communications, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, has described threats to kill President John Dramani Mahama and his children as “brazen criminality”, insisting that such conduct must not be defended in the name of free expression. Speaking on behalf of the President at the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards in Accra, he urged political leaders not to support threats and incitement to violence for partisan advantage. “For instance, threatening to kill a president and his children is not free speech. It is brazen criminality. We, as political leaders, must not lend support to this level of criminality only because it enures to the benefits of our political fortunes,” he said. Mr Kwakye Ofosu said political leaders must demonstrate consistency in their defence of free speech, particularly when journalists face threats for publishing critical or uncomfortable reports. “Our words in support of free speech must not ring hollow, especially when in the north, in the past, journalists had to flee our country for fear of their lives because they published uncomfortable truths,” he stated. The Minister stressed that efforts to combat hate speech should not become a justification for restricting dissent, critical journalism or unpopular opinions. He said democracy depended on the freedom to disagree, but should not accommodate deliberate incitement of hatred, violence and intolerance. “Democracy thrives on disagreement, and what it cannot accommodate is the deliberate incitement of hatred, violence, and intolerance. A clear distinction must be struck between criminal conduct and the expression of free speech,” he said. The comments were made at the 30th GJA Media Awards, held under the theme, “Celebrating Excellence, Advancing Media Freedom and Combating Hate Speech in the Digital Age.” The event brought together journalists, media organisations and other stakeholders to recognise excellence in journalism and discuss issues affecting media freedom.

Kébémer : le bilan du présumé naufrage d’une pirogue passe à 21 morts
items.description: Le bilan du présumé naufrage d’une pirogue transportant des candidats à l’émigration irrégulière s’est alourdi, passant de quatre à 21 morts. Ce samedi, les côtes de Loumpoul, dans le département de Kébémer, offrent un spectacle particulièrement macabre. Les corps sans vie sont alignés les uns à côté des autres sur la rive. Les éléments de la gendarmerie et les sapeurs-pompiers poursuivent les opérations de recherche, dans l’espoir de retrouver d’autres victimes. Selon notre source, la plupart des victimes seraient originaires des communes de Léona et de Thiéppe. Cette tragédie plonge les populations dans l’émoi et la consternation. Pour l’heure, les dépouilles sont acheminées vers le district sanitaire de Kébémer. Ces derniers temps, le phénomène de l’émigration irrégulière, avec son lot de conséquences tragiques, prend de plus en plus d’ampleur. Face à cette problématique persistante, il devient urgent de trouver des solutions durables pour endiguer ce fléau. Falel Pam

items.title: UPLG : Minkailou Barry élu président de l’Union de la Presse Libre de Guinée
items.description: Ce samedi 7 novembre 2026 à Conakry, Minkailou Barry est élu président de l'Union de la Presse Libre de Guinée (UPLG). Il a remporté l'élection présidentielle de l'association, organisée lors de son congrès à la Maison de la Presse de Guinée. Directeur de publication du site leverificateur.net, M. Barry occupait jusque-là le poste de secrétaire général de l'organisation. Il affrontait Mohamed Cissé, directeur de publication du média en ligne avenirguinee.org. Le vote s'est soldé par 44 voix pour M. Barry et 14 pour son adversaire. Un bulletin a été déclaré nul. L'huissier de justice, Me Amadou Soumah, a proclamé les résultats devant l'assemblée. La salle était pleine. Journalistes, directeurs de publication et autres acteurs des médias avaient fait le déplacement. Le nouveau président remplace Grégoire Ankou, qui quitte la tête de l'UPLG. Les congressistes ont salué son bilan. Sous sa direction, l'organisation est passée d'une dizaine de membres en 2019 à près d'une centaine aujourd'hui. Après la proclamation, Minkailou Barry a remercié l'ensemble des membres. Il a salué les membres de l'intérieur du pays, notamment ceux de Kankan, ainsi que ceux installés à l'étranger pour leur mobilisation malgré la distance géopolitique. Il a rendu hommage aux pionniers de l'UPLG, dont l'honorable Bahfisher et Ibrahima Koné. Il a également salué le travail de Grégoire Ankou et l'attitude démocratique de son challenger Mohamed Cissé. Le président élu a insisté sur la cohésion de l'organisation. « Il n'y a pas d'UPLG du candidat A, ni d'UPLG du candidat B. L'UPLG est une et indivisible », a-t-il déclaré. Le bureau exécutif compte 11 membres. Il a fixé trois axes de travail, face aux enjeux du numérique, de l'intelligence artificielle et de l'équilibre financier des rédactions. Le premier axe concerne la formation continue et la déontologie. L'objectif est de renforcer les compétences des journalistes et de garantir une information rigoureuse. Le deuxième porte sur la viabilité économique. L'UPLG veut conclure des partenariats pour structurer les rédactions et améliorer les conditions de travail dans les entreprises de presse membres. Le troisième vise la solidarité et la protection des membres. L'organisation entend soutenir juridiquement et moralement les directeurs de publication et les journalistes, à Conakry, à l'intérieur du pays et à l'étranger. Minkailou Barry a conclu son intervention sous les applaudissements. « Le temps des discours est fini, l'heure est à l'action », a-t-il affirmé. L’article UPLG : Minkailou Barry élu président de l'Union de la Presse Libre de Guinée est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Maison Kanty's, la mode ivoirienne tissée de souvenirs et de savoir-faire
items.description: William Mackenzie, cofondateur et directeur artistique de la marque ivoirienne Maison Kanty's, crée avec Thierry Aguy des collections inspirées de leur vécu et de leur héritage culturel. items.title: CIIE 2026 | Promotion de l’artisanat tunisien et recherche de partenariats durables en Chine
items.description: La participation de la Tunisie à la 9e édition de l'Exposition internationale des importations de la Chine (CIIE 2026) à Shanghai, du 5 au 10 novembre 2026, met en lumière la richesse de son artisanat et ouvre de nouvelles perspectives sur le marché chinois. Organisée en collaboration avec l'ambassade de Tunisie à Pékin et l'Office national de l'artisanat tunisien, cette initiative vise à promouvoir le savoir-faire local et à renforcer les échanges commerciaux. Le pavillon tunisien expose des produits artisanaux de haute qualité qui reflètent la créativité des artisans et la diversité du patrimoine culturel national, indique l'Office national en précisant que cet événement constitue une vitrine stratégique pour attirer les investisseurs et les importateurs chinois, facilitant l'accès des produits tunisiens aux marchés internationaux. La même source affirme par ailleurs que cette démarche renforce la coopération bilatérale et ouvre la voie à des partenariats commerciaux durables entre la Tunisie et la Chine. Y. N. L’article CIIE 2026 | Promotion de l'artisanat tunisien et recherche de partenariats durables en Chine est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Surf : l'incroyable expédition des "Lost in the Swell" au cercle arctique
items.description: Depuis 15 ans, Lost in the Swell sillonne la planète à la recherche de spots de surf reculés et encore vierges. Pour cette nouvelle expédition "Le Règne des Neiges", le trio est parti au cercle arctique avec l’espoir de découvrir des vagues encore jamais surfées. Partis en mars 2026, ils ont vécu un mois et demi d’expédition dans des conditions particulièrement engagées : fenêtres météo très courtes, eau à 3 °C et températures ressenties jusqu’à -15 °C.

items.title: Finances publiques : le parlement fixe un cap d’urgence et d’efficacité pour le budget 2026
items.description: A la suite de l'examen minutieux du volet dépenses du projet de loi de finances rectificative (PLFR) 2026, l'Assemblée nationale a formulé, ce samedi 7 novembre, une série de recommandations stratégiques pour redresser l'exécution budgétaire et garantir un impact concret sur le quotidien des populations. Au cœur des préoccupation figure le constat alarmant du faible taux d'exécution des dépenses d'investissement, où 75 % des départements ministériels affichent un taux de paiement inférieur à 30 %. Face à cette inertie administrative, le Parlement invite le Premier ministre à diligenter une évaluation approfondie pour situer les responsabilités et exige la mise en place d'un mécanisme d'évaluation trimestrielle des investissements assorti de rapports semestriels. Pour garantir la dignité des travailleurs des Établissements Publics à Caractère Administratif (EPA) frappés par des arriérés de paiement, la représentation nationale recommande la création d'un mécanisme de sécurisation et de réservation préalable des crédits salariaux dès le vote du budget. Sur le plan de la transparence et de la gestion de la dette publique, la représentation nationale demande de clore les audits de la dette intérieure sur la période 2014-2020 en y associant l'Ordre des experts-comptables de Guinée, tout en procédant au paiement direct des créances postérieures régulièrement ordonnancées. Pour lutter contre les risques de surfacturation et encadrer les coûts des infrastructures, l'actualisation et l'élargissement de la mercuriale des prix par l'Institut National de la Statistique (INS) ainsi que l'établissement d'un référentiel propre aux travaux routiers par l'AGEROUTE sont vivement préconisés. En parallèle, des mesures d'urgence écologique et économique sont sollicitées, à l'image de la protection des mangroves et du développement d'infrastructures pour les PME et l'artisanat. Le développement territorial et l'équité sociale occupent également une place prépondérante dans ces orientations parlementaires. L'Assemblée nationale insiste sur l'accélération du désenclavement rural, recommandant la construction d'au moins 1 000 kilomètres de pistes en 2027 et 1 400 kilomètres en 2028 pour atteindre les objectifs du Programme Simandou 2040. Face à la retenue injustifiée des fonds alloués à l'ANAFIC — avec seulement 0,65 % des ressources rétrocédées aux collectivités —, le Parlement réclame une procédure d'exécution spéciale garantissant une allocation annuelle minimale d'au moins 2 300 milliards GNF aux collectivités locales. La coordination interministérielle est appelée à se renforcer pour éviter les blocages de chantiers routiers dus au déplacement des réseaux publics. La rationalisation des charges de l'État s'accompagne d'exigences fortes dans le secteur de l'énergie et de la souveraineté numérique. Le Parlement invite le Gouvernement à encadrer progressivement les subventions accordées à Électricité de Guinée (EDG), tout en exigeant l'électrification intégrale des localités riveraines des barrages de Kaléta, Souapiti et Amaria dès 2027. Pour sécuriser les télécommunications nationales, l'investissement dans un second câble sous-marin est recommandé afin d'éliminer tout risque de rupture de connectivité. La diplomatie n'est pas en reste, avec l'invitation à assurer le paiement régulier des cotisations internationales et la modernisation des représentations diplomatiques. Les réformes d'inclusion et de modernisation administrative font l'objet d'un suivi strict. L'Assemblée exige l'aménagement systématique de passerelles et d'infrastructures accessibles aux personnes en situation de handicap, la redynamisation du Fonds de garantie pour le secteur privé, et le respect du délai légal de 24 heures par la Banque centrale (BCRG) pour le traitement des ordres de virement afin de ne pas paralyser l'économie. De plus, elle demande une double liquidation systématique pour sécuriser les recettes des Budgets d'Affectation Spéciale (BAS), l'organisation d'une retraite nationale pour simplifier la chaîne de dépense, ainsi que le décaissement en urgence des crédits dédiés aux cantines scolaires. Enfin, sur le plan des projets majeurs, le rapport recommande d'insérer des clauses de délais impératifs dans les conventions avec les bailleurs de fonds (FINEX), de respecter scrupuleusement les plafonds budgétaires votés, et d'accélérer la construction de salles de classe et de centres de santé. Dans le cadre du Programme Simandou 2040, le Parlement appelle à renforcer la maturité des projets via l'Agence de contrôle des grands projets (ACGP), à préserver les terres agricoles du corridor Simandou et à créer une société nationale de transport public urbain et interurbain. Pour conclure, le rapport insiste sur la finalisation des infrastructures administratives et judiciaires, le soutien au patrimoine culturel national, et la satisfaction stricte de tous les préalables légaux avant la généralisation du budget-programme prévue pour 2027.

items.title: Simandou Mining Summit: Mamadi Doumbouya lance l’appel qui va consacrer le réveil économique de la Guinée
items.description: Avec le Simandou Mining Sommit prévu du 11 au 14 novembre à Conakry la Guinée a décidé de frachir un nouveau cape dans sa conquête du monde des affaires. C’est pourquoi, dans une publication officielle pour la circonstance, en prélude à cet événement d'envergure, le président de la République déclare que: «Le monde a rendez-vous en République de Guinée. » Une phrase courte, mais vibrante, qui sonne comme une invitation solennelle autant que comme la réaffirmation du leadership retrouvé sur la scène économique continentale. En tout cas, «Le 11 novembre 2026, sur l’île de Kassa, s’ouvrira la 𝟭ʳᵉ 𝗲́𝗱𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗱𝘂 𝗦𝗶𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗼𝘂 𝗠𝗶𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗦𝘂𝗺𝗺𝗶𝘁, placée sous le thème : « 𝗟’𝗶𝗻𝗱𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗲 𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗶𝗲̀𝗿𝗲, 𝗺𝗼𝘁𝗲𝘂𝗿 𝗱𝗲 𝗹𝗮 𝗱𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗶𝗳𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗲́𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗼𝗺𝗶𝗾𝘂𝗲 𝗮̀ 𝗹’𝗲̀𝗿𝗲 𝗱𝗲 𝗦𝗶𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗼𝘂 𝟮𝟬𝟰𝟬 », rappelle-t-il. Poursuivant son message, le chef de l’Etat note «qu’il y a un an, Simandou entrait en exploitation». Et «qu’Aujourd’hui, la Guinée franchit une nouvelle étape : 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗲𝗿 𝘀𝗲𝘀 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗲𝘀 𝗲𝗻 𝗶𝗻𝗱𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗲𝘀, 𝗲𝗻 𝗲𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗼𝗶𝘀 𝗲𝘁 𝗲𝗻 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘀𝗽𝗲́𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗲́ 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗮𝗴𝗲́𝗲». C’est pourquoi, explique l’actuel locateur du palais Mohamed V, «j’𝗶𝗻𝘃𝗶𝘁𝗲 𝗹𝗲𝘀 𝗶𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘂𝗿𝘀, 𝗹𝗲𝘀 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗲𝗻𝗮𝗶𝗿𝗲𝘀 𝗲𝘁 𝗹𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗺𝗶𝘀 𝗱𝗲 𝗹𝗮 𝗚𝘂𝗶𝗻𝗲́𝗲 𝗮̀ 𝘃𝗲𝗻𝗶𝗿 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗽𝗮𝗿 𝗲𝘂𝘅-𝗺𝗲̂𝗺𝗲𝘀 𝗹𝗮 𝗻𝗼𝘂𝘃𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗲 𝗱𝘆𝗻𝗮𝗺𝗶𝗾𝘂𝗲 𝗱𝗲 𝗱𝗲́𝘃𝗲𝗹𝗼𝗽𝗽𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 de notre pays». Et de terminier son message par la formule percutante, « GUINEA IS OPEN FOR BUSINESS », le président Doumbouya tend la main pour un partenariat pupblic privé gagant gagant dans une Guinée résolument tournée vers l'avenir.

items.title: Orpailleurs refoulés de Guinée : Près de 160 000 personnes accueillies à Bamako et Kouremalé, six décès enregistrés
items.description: Le Centre de coordination et de gestion des crises (CECOGEC) au Mali à fait le bilan des mesures prises à la date du 07 novembre 2026, face à l'afflux de milliers d'orpailleurs refoulés de Guinée. Selon le communiqué à cette date, environ 160 000 personnes ont été recensées, dont près de 100 000 dans le district de Bamako et 60 000 à Kouremalé. Le bilan fait également état de plusieurs blessés et de six décès enregistrés à Kouremalé, Face à cette situation exceptionnelle, le gouvernement malien a engagé, à travers le Comité interministériel de gestion des crises et catastrophes, plusieurs mesures d'urgence pour assurer l'accueil, la sécurisation et l'assistance des personnes concernées, ainsi que l'organisation de leur retour dans leurs pays respectifs. Parmi les principales dispositions prises figure l'aménagement et la sécurisation d'un site d'accueil d'urgence à Quinzinbougou. Les autorités ont également mobilisé l'ensemble des départements ministériels afin de coordonner les opérations sur le terrain. Selon le communiqué, dans le cadre de l'organisation des retours, le Burkina Faso a mis à disposition 47 bus, auxquels se sont ajoutés deux bus mobilisés par le Mali. Ce dispositif a permis le retour de près de 3 430 personnes le 5 novembre 2026. Le lendemain, le Mali a déployé 74 camions et 24 bus pour assurer le convoyage d'environ 15 000 personnes vers le Burkina Faso. Les opérations d’embarquement se sont poursuivies le 7 novembre avec la mobilisation de 60 camions et 10 bus par les autorités maliennes, ainsi que de 48 cars par le Burkina Faso. Sur le plan sanitaire, 413 personnes refoulées ont bénéficié d'une prise en charge dans différentes structures de santé du district de Bamako. Une importante mobilisation citoyenne et communautaire accompagne également les opérations. Elle implique notamment les jeunes, les travailleurs sociaux, les opérateurs économiques et les personnes de bonne volonté, qui apportent leur soutien aux actions d'assistance. Dans son communiqué, le CECOGEC adresse ses condoléances aux familles des six personnes décédées, exprime sa compassion aux personnes affectées et souhaite un prompt rétablissement aux blessés. Le Centre appelle par ailleurs les autorités régionales à maintenir un niveau maximal de mobilisation et de vigilance pour garantir le bon déroulement des opérations d'accueil, d'identification, d'enregistrement, d'assistance et de retour des personnes refoulées. Enfin, il remercie les populations et les différents acteurs pour leur élan de solidarité, tout en rappelant que les dons et autres formes d'appui doivent être coordonnés avec les structures techniques compétentes afin d'en assurer une gestion efficace et une répartition appropriée. items.title: Guinée : les députés approuvent un budget rectifié de 67 925,87 milliards GNF pour 2026
items.description: L’Assemblée nationale guinéenne a adopté, ce samedi 7 novembre 2026, en séance plénière, le volet Dépenses du Projet de Loi de Finances Rectificative (PLFR) pour l’exercice 2026. Présenté par le rapporteur général, N’Gouamou Fabara Koné, au nom de la Commission des Affaires économiques et financières, du Plan et de la Coopération, le rapport soumis aux députés vient clôturer les travaux parlementaires intensifs conduits du 1er au 5 novembre dernier. Des dépenses en hausse de 5,83 %, tirées par les charges courantes Les prévisions de dépenses de l’État pour 2026 sont désormais fixées à 67 925,87 milliards GNF, contre 64 181,37 milliards GNF dans la Loi de finances initiale (LFI). Cela représente une augmentation de 3 744,50 milliards GNF, soit une progression de 5,83 %. Cette révision à la hausse s’explique essentiellement par les ajustements opérés sur le Budget général, notamment au niveau des dépenses courantes, qui enregistrent une progression de 18,06 % pour atteindre 41 954,40 milliards GNF. Cette augmentation est principalement portée par les dépenses de transfert, en hausse de 66,84 %. Elle tient notamment à la prise en charge des pertes de recettes pétrolières, évaluées à 4 576,7 milliards GNF, afin de maintenir le prix du carburant à la pompe à 12 000 GNF. À cela s’ajoute une provision de 913 milliards GNF destinée à la stabilisation des hydrocarbures. Les dépenses de personnel sont, quant à elles, évaluées à 12 629,84 milliards GNF, soit une hausse de 1,02 %. Cette enveloppe intègre notamment 250 milliards GNF de primes de performance au profit de la Direction générale des impôts, ainsi que la prise en charge, à compter d’août 2026, de 939 nouveaux agents de police. De leur côté, les dépenses de biens et services s’établissent à 9 659,67 milliards GNF, en progression de 9,98 %. Cette évolution prend notamment en compte le reliquat des dépenses liées à l’organisation des élections législatives et communales, estimé à 367,15 milliards GNF. En revanche, les charges financières de la dette connaissent une baisse de 19,48 %, pour s’établir à 3 836,58 milliards GNF. Cette diminution résulte de l’actualisation des échéanciers de paiement des intérêts de la dette intérieure et extérieure. Les investissements revus à la baisse, le déficit contenu À l’inverse de la tendance observée pour les dépenses courantes, les dépenses d’investissement du Budget général ont été revues à la baisse. Elles s’établissent désormais à 23 562,27 milliards GNF, soit un recul de 10,13 %, correspondant à une diminution de 2 655,80 milliards GNF par rapport aux prévisions initiales. Selon les éléments présentés dans le rapport, cette contraction s’explique principalement par le report à 2027 du démarrage de certains projets dont le niveau de maturation a été jugé insuffisant. Ces dépenses d’investissement se répartissent entre les projets, pour une enveloppe de 20 015,98 milliards GNF, et les investissements hors projets, évalués à 3 546,28 milliards GNF. Cette dernière rubrique comprend notamment le Fonds d’entretien routier et divers équipements publics. Pour leur part, les Budgets d’affectation spéciale (BAS) enregistrent une légère baisse de 0,70 %, pour se chiffrer à 2 409,20 milliards GNF. Ils se répartissent entre le Fonds national de développement local (FNDL), avec 1 114,44 milliards GNF, le FODECCON (708,26 milliards GNF), le Fonds d'investissement minier (FIM), doté de 371,48 milliards GNF, et le Fonds commun de l'éducation (FCE), avec 215,02 milliards GNF. Au terme de ces réajustements, le solde budgétaire global affiche un déficit de 7 861,40 milliards GNF, soit l’équivalent de 2,01 % du PIB, contre un taux initial de 2,07 %. Le rapport prévoit que ce déficit sera intégralement couvert par des opérations de financement intérieur et extérieur. Simandou 2040 au cœur des arbitrages budgétaires Autre élément mis en avant dans le rapport : l’alignement du PLFR 2026 sur le Programme Simandou 2040, consacré par la loi-plan du 5 mars 2026. Sur les 339 projets identifiés dans ce programme stratégique, 176 sont directement inscrits dans le présent collectif budgétaire, pour une enveloppe globale de 10 137,65 milliards GNF. Ce montant représente 43,61 % de l’ensemble des dépenses d’investissement de l’État, tandis que le taux d’alignement du portefeuille de projets atteint 52 %. Par ailleurs, afin de mieux prendre en compte certaines priorités sectorielles et d’ajuster la répartition des ressources publiques, la commission de fond a introduit plusieurs amendements budgétaires ciblés. Dans le secteur de l’éducation et de l’enseignement supérieur, 40 milliards GNF ont été inscrits pour le paiement partiel des travaux de l’Université Gamal Abdel Nasser de Conakry, auxquels s’ajoutent 24,3 milliards GNF en faveur de l’Université Général Lansana Conté de Sonfonia. Dans le domaine de l’industrie et de l’appui aux petites et moyennes entreprises (PME), les amendements prévoient 15 milliards GNF pour la construction de centres régionaux d’appui aux PME et 6 milliards GNF pour le Fonds de développement industriel. D’autres dotations concernent le développement et la sécurité. Il s’agit notamment de 6,425 milliards GNF accordés au Service national d’aménagement des points d’eau (SNAPE) pour l’acquisition de camions-citernes, de 15 milliards GNF destinés à couvrir les frais du concours de recrutement dans la Fonction publique, ainsi que du renforcement des crédits consacrés au contrôle minier et aux équipements judiciaires.

items.title: Kankan : un incendie ravage un atelier de menuiserie à Farako 2, plus de 100 millions de GNF de pertes estimées
items.description: Un important incendie s'est déclaré dans la soirée à Farako 2, dans la commune urbaine de Kankan, ravageant un atelier de menuiserie et plusieurs équipements de travail. Le bilan matériel est estimé à plus de 100 millions de francs guinéens par le promoteur de l'atelier. Aucune perte en vie humaine ni blessure n'a été signalée. Selon les premiers témoignages, le feu serait parti d'un court-circuit au niveau d'un dynamo. L'intervention des sapeurs-pompiers a toutefois été marquée par des tensions avec certains habitants, qui auraient lancé des pierres sur les agents de secours. ‎ ‎Les flammes ont rapidement gagné l'intérieur de l'atelier, consumant plusieurs équipements, des meubles et d'importants stocks de bois destinés à la fabrication. Selon Mamadou Samba Sow, promoteur de l'atelier, le sinistre s'est déclaré alors que les ouvriers étaient en plein travail. ‎ ‎« On était en train de travailler lorsque le dynamo a fait un court-circuit. Le feu a directement pris les tôles. C'est ainsi qu'on a fait sortir les enfants de l'atelier, qui sont des apprentis. Alhamdoulillah, rien n'est arrivé à quelqu'un, mais les machines et les bois ont été consumés », explique-t-il. ‎ ‎Le promoteur estime les pertes à plus de 100 millions de francs guinéens. Quatre machines, un moteur et le dynamo figurent parmi les équipements détruits. Des meubles, des portes, des armoires ainsi que des bois en cours de préparation sont également partis en fumée. ‎ ‎Face à l'ampleur des dégâts, Mamadou Samba Sow lance un appel à la solidarité pour pouvoir relancer ses activités. Il rappelle que son atelier fait travailler plus de 30 personnes. ‎ ‎« Que tout le monde m'aide. Aidez-moi à avoir des machines, puisqu'il y a plus de 30 personnes qui travaillent ici », plaide-t-il. ‎ ‎Des tensions lors de l'intervention des sapeurs-pompiers ‎ ‎Alors que les secours étaient mobilisés pour maîtriser les flammes, leur intervention a été perturbée par des tensions avec une partie de la population. qui a lancé des pierres contre. Selon Mohamed Savané, qui affirme avoir été alerté par un membre du bureau de quartier, les sapeurs-pompiers ont été contactés à plusieurs reprises avant leur arrivée sur les lieux. ‎ ‎Mais une fois sur place, certains habitants, visiblement mécontents, auraient commencé à jeter des pierres sur les agents, les obligeant à interrompre momentanément leurs opérations. ‎ ‎« J'ai appelé les sapeurs-pompiers plus de dix fois. Ils ont répondu à l'appel et sont venus. Mais, vu que les gens étaient tellement énervés, certains ont commencé à leur jeter des pierres. C'est ce qui a fait dégénérer la situation », témoigne Mohamed Savané. ‎ ‎Face à cette situation, il affirme avoir pris contact avec les responsables de l'équipe de secours afin de les convaincre de revenir sur les lieux. Une démarche qui aurait permis la reprise de l'intervention. ‎ ‎Les sapeurs-pompiers appellent à la compréhension ‎ ‎De leur côté, les agents des sapeurs-pompiers regrettent cette attitude de la population et rappellent que leurs moyens d'intervention sont destinés à protéger les populations. ‎ ‎« Je m'adresse personnellement à la population de Kankan. Nos camions sont pour elle, pas pour nous. Nous travaillons pour la population et nous sommes là pour accomplir notre mission. Ce n'est pas de notre faute si certaines situations se produisent », explique un agent intervenu sur les lieux. ‎ ‎Il invite les habitants à mieux comprendre les conditions dans lesquelles les équipes de secours travaillent. Selon lui, la rapidité de l'intervention dépend notamment du moment où l'alerte est donnée, de la localisation du sinistre et de l'ampleur des flammes. ‎ ‎L'agent insiste ainsi sur la nécessité d'alerter les secours dès les premiers signes d'incendie et de leur communiquer des indications précises pour faciliter leur déplacement. ‎ ‎Ibrahima Barry, l'un des apprentis de l'atelier, regrette également la réaction de certains habitants. Informé de l'incendie alors qu'il ne se trouvait pas sur les lieux, il affirme s'être rendu au poste des sapeurs-pompiers pour accompagner leur déplacement. ‎ ‎« Quand j'ai été informé, je me suis dirigé vers le local des sapeurs-pompiers. Ils étaient en préparation et nous sommes venus ensemble. Mais la foule s'est révoltée. S'ils avaient pu travailler, l'ampleur des dégâts ne serait peut-être pas aussi importante. Mais chacun a sa façon de voir les choses », témoigne-t-il. ‎ ‎Il affirme avoir ensuite participé aux démarches visant à convaincre les agents de revenir, avec l'appui du responsable de l'atelier. ‎ ‎À Farako 2, cet incendie laisse derrière lui d'importantes pertes matérielles et un atelier à reconstruire. Le promoteur espère désormais bénéficier d'un élan de solidarité pour retrouver son outil de travail et permettre aux dizaines de personnes qui en dépendent de reprendre leurs activités. L'épisode rappelle également l'importance de préserver les conditions d'intervention des équipes de secours en période d'urgence. ‎ Karifa Kansan Doumbouya correspondant à Kankan L’article Kankan : un incendie ravage un atelier de menuiserie à Farako 2, plus de 100 millions de GNF de pertes estimées est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .
